item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Porsche (P911_p.DE) is aiming for a group operating return on sales of 15% in the long term, the German sports car maker and Volkswagen subsidiary said on Wednesday, as it presents a [USN:L8N45S1JL TEXT:"turnaround strategy"] to compensate for lower sales with profit-boosting luxury. In the medium term, the company is aiming for an operating margin in the range of 10 to 15%, it said in a statement.

item.title: La caída de los bonos no deja margen a Francia para errores fiscales, dice ejecutivo de Citadel
item.description: Francia ya no tiene margen de error para sanear sus finanzas públicas, y la presión de los mercados financieros debería contribuir a que en París se centren en contener el gasto de cara a las elecciones presidenciales del año que viene, dijo a Reuters Ángel Ubide, alto ejecutivo de Citadel.
item.dc:creator: Leigh Thomas, Gabriel Stargardter
item.content:encoded: Francia ya no tiene margen de error para sanear sus finanzas públicas, y la presión de los mercados financieros debería contribuir a que en París se centren en contener el gasto de cara a las elecciones presidenciales del año que viene, dijo a Reuters Ángel Ubide, alto ejecutivo de Citadel. Francia ha visto cómo se disparaban sus costos de financiación en la actual caída global de los mercados de bonos, lo que ha provocado una ola de ventas del euro, ya que a los inversores les preocupa que la fragilidad de sus finanzas públicas pueda extenderse al resto de Europa. Ubide, director de Investigación Económica para Renta Fija y Macroeconomía en Citadel, que gestiona activos por valor de 76.000 millones de dólares, dijo que Francia no supone un riesgo sistémico para Europa… todavía. "Francia es un país muy grande. Si hablamos de un problema sistémico en Francia, estamos hablando de un problema sistémico para Europa. Espero y confío en que no lleguemos al punto de tener que abordar ese debate", dijo Ubide a Reuters en una entrevista. Además de las elecciones presidenciales, también es fundamental que las elecciones parlamentarias den lugar a una mayoría capaz de controlar las finanzas públicas, señaló Ubide. "Por eso creo que la presión del mercado, en ese sentido, es útil, porque envía una señal clara de que no hay margen para el error. Eso es lo más importante", dijo. Las turbulencias en el mercado de bonos francés han suscitado preocupación en los mercados financieros por la posibilidad de que provoquen un efecto dominó que afecte a otros países de la zona del euro y a la propia moneda. Responsables del [USN:L6N45S0LT TEXT:"BCE"] y el ministro de Economía francés han descartado hasta ahora que sea necesario que el Banco Central Europeo intervenga para estabilizar el mercado. El rendimiento de los bonos franceses a 10 años alcanzó brevemente la semana pasada su máximo en 24 años, situándose por encima del 5%. Mientras tanto, el euro alcanzó el lunes mínimos de 17 meses, por debajo de 1,12 dólares , y se desplomó frente a la libra esterlina , el franco suizo y el yen japonés . LAS ELECCIONES Y LAS PROTESTAS AUMENTAN LA INESTABILIDAD Las elecciones presidenciales francesas se acercan en un contexto de protestas estudiantiles, subida de precios y dificultades económicas, lo que lleva a los votantes descontentos a abandonar los partidos mayoritarios en favor de los de extrema derecha y extrema izquierda, que están ganando terreno en las encuestas. Marine Le Pen, la candidata de extrema derecha que lidera las encuestas, intentó el martes reforzar su credibilidad en materia presupuestaria, comprometiéndose a un fuerte aumento de sus planes de recorte del gasto si resulta elegida. Le Pen afirmó que se fijaría como objetivo un ahorro presupuestario de 140.000 millones de euros (157.600 millones de dólares) a lo largo de un mandato presidencial de cinco años y que consagraría la reducción del déficit en la Constitución mediante un referéndum. Sin embargo, sus propuestas han sido recibidas con escepticismo por parte de los economistas con los que habló Reuters. Estos cuestionaron que se pudieran lograr recortes de tal magnitud, sobre todo porque dio pocos detalles sobre si tiene previsto mantener la política de reducir la edad de jubilación para algunos trabajadores. "Sigue habiendo una gran incógnita: ¿quién es la verdadera Marine Le Pen? Todavía estamos conociéndola, y el mercado tardará en formarse una opinión", dijo Ubide. (1 dólar = 0,8883 euros)

item.title: Australian uranium miners rally after Google's power deal with Constellation Energy
item.description: Australian uranium miners logged their best session in weeks on Wednesday after Alphabet's Google agreed to buy power from US nuclear energy major Constellation Energy , potentially raising the demand for uranium.
item.dc:creator: Keshav Singhchundawat, Jasmeen Shaikh
item.content:encoded: Australian uranium miners logged their best session in weeks on Wednesday after Alphabet's Google (GOOGL.O) agreed to [USN:L6N45S0XB TEXT:"buy power"] from US nuclear energy major Constellation Energy (CEG.O) , potentially raising the demand for uranium. Here are the details: Boss Energy (BOE.AX) rose 4.6%, clocking its biggest intraday gain in over a week Deep Yellow (DYL.AX) gained 4.6% in its best session since September 3. Paladin Energy (PDN.AX) advanced 2.5%, logging its biggest gain in more than two weeks. The global data centre boom is straining power and water infrastructure, pushing operators and hyperscalers to prioritise sustainability. It is also boosting interest in nuclear energy as a reliable low-carbon power source. Google on Tuesday inked a 20-year agreement for 890 megawatts of electricity — about a quarter of total contracted capacity — from multiple Constellation-owned nuclear power plants, which would be upgraded to produce more electricity from existing reactors. "The Google-Constellation Energy deal is giving the entire uranium complex a spike," said Luke Winchester, portfolio manager at Merewether Capital. The uranium bulls have called for nuclear to be the primary energy source for power-intensive data centres, and the validation of one of the world's largest hyperscalers is giving those arguments legitimacy, Winchester added.

item.title: Shell raises Q3 gas output forecast
item.description: Shell's third-quarter integrated gas production was expected to be about 740,000 to 780,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, the company said on Wednesday, compared with a previously expected a range of 570,000 to 630,000 boed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shell's (SHEL.L) third-quarter integrated gas production was expected to be about 740,000 to 780,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, the company said on Wednesday, compared with a previously expected a range of 570,000 to 630,000 boed. In the second quarter the company produced 631,000 boed in comparison with over 900,000 boed before the US and Israel started a war on Iran in February. Third-quarter LNG production was expected to be about 7.2 million to 7.6 million metric tons, the company said, compared with a previous forecast of 7.1 million to 7.7 million tons and compared to 7.7 million tons in the second quarter. The integrated gas outlook includes its $16.4 billion [USN:L6N41A0R1 TEXT:"acquisition"] of Canadian energy company ARC resources, which completed on September 2, the oil major said.

item.title: IMF chief warns energy shock, growing debt and AI risks threaten global growth
item.description: The global economy is under threat from persistently high energy prices, record public debt and risks from the AI investment boom, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned on Wednesday, urging governments to take protective fiscal and monetary policy measures.
item.dc:creator: Rae Wee
item.content:encoded: The global economy is under threat from persistently high energy prices, record public debt and risks from the AI investment boom, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned on Wednesday, urging governments to take protective fiscal and monetary policy measures. In a speech previewing IMF and World Bank Annual Meetings next week in Bangkok, Georgieva said the world was being pulled in two directions -- a negative energy supply shock from the Middle East conflicts and a positive demand shock from artificial intelligence that is also fuelling inflation. "The combined impact of these two forces is highly uneven across the world," Georgieva said, adding that the AI boom was bypassing many countries. New IMF growth forecasts to be released during the Bangkok meetings will show the biggest growth downgrades will come in economies ravaged by war, Georgieva said. These include Ukraine, suffering significant damage to civilian and economic infrastructure, and Gulf countries hit by Iranian strikes and sharply reduced energy exports. Georgieva did not indicate in her prepared remarks whether the IMF's latest World Economic Outlook would change the overall 2026 global growth forecast from the sluggish 3.0% rate [USN:L1N439118 TEXT:"forecast in July"]. That forecast, which predicted a rebound to 3.4% growth in 2027, assumed the Strait of Hormuz would start to reopen in mid-July and return to pre-war conditions by March 2027. It assumed oil prices would average $89 a barrel in 2026 and $78 a barrel in 2027. Georgieva said oil prices remain at $100 a barrel, with impaired refining capacity adding another $100 in "crack-spread" margins per barrel for key products including diesel. The winter heating season will boost demand as natural gas supplies remain restricted by threats to LNG shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, she added. "Even if the war in the Gulf were to end soon, the problem of high energy prices will likely persist for some time," Georgieva said, adding that Brent crude oil futures predict high oil prices through 2027. Higher energy prices are pushing up inflation, policy rates and benchmark bond yields, she said, noting that US, German and Japanese 10-year sovereign yields are now at their highest levels since 2007, 2009 and 1996, respectively, and still climbing. GROWING DEBT LOAD Adding to the worries to be discussed by the IMF's 191 member countries next week is a growing public debt burden that is sapping growth and adding inflationary pressures, Georgieva said. The IMF says public debt is at the highest level since World War Two and is projected to exceed 100% of GDP before 2030. Georgieva singled out advanced economies, led by the United States, as the "worst offenders" on debt loads, with debt-to-GDP ratios higher than emerging markets and low income countries. Policymakers can no longer rely on higher growth rates alone to solve fiscal problems, she said. "And yet we don't see decisive action in the high-debt advanced economies where the need of the hour is for credible medium-term fiscal consolidation plans, supported in some cases by upfront fiscal measures, including to take some pressure off monetary policy," she said. After five-and-a-half years of above-target inflation, Georgieva said inflationary pressures were persisting, from the AI build-out, energy and food price shocks, tariffs, higher defense spending and higher debt service costs. "Now may be a good time for a prudently hawkish bias in many countries' monetary policy," Georgieva said, adding that rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve, the ECB and the Bank of Japan were "highly appropriate." AI RISKS ABOUND Georgieva highlighted other risks from AI, where investment as a share of GDP is [USN:L6N45N0Q6 TEXT:"likely to exceed"] that of railroads, the electricity grids or telecommunications infrastructure. The rising economic and financial concentration puts pressure on AI companies to deliver productivity and earnings gains to justify lofty valuations, she said, warning that market disappointment could turn into "a far-reaching shock." But she said IMF research suggests that AI, done right, could add a half percentage point of extra world growth annually. AI preparedness is key, she said, including regulatory guardrails that "help manage AI's substantial perils, which include large-scale labor market fallout, serious cyber and stability risks and frontier models threatening to escape human control and run amok." In addition to building fiscal strength, even at difficult political costs, Georgieva said governments should take other steps to boost growth, including reforms that would develop improved workforce skills, make corporate start-ups and wind-downs easier, boost energy security and streamline regulations.

item.title: Porsche braces for lower sales era, seeks lifeline from luxury
item.description: Porsche is steeling itself for persistently lower sales, the Volkswagen brand said on Wednesday, pitching a turnaround plan to investors that aims to boost margins with a focus on top-end models.
item.dc:creator: Rachel More, Ilona Wissenbach
item.content:encoded: Porsche (P911_p.DE) is steeling itself for persistently lower sales, the Volkswagen brand said on Wednesday, pitching a [USN:L8N45S1Q7 TEXT:"turnaround plan"] to investors that aims to boost margins with a focus on top-end models. The sports car maker, which, like parent Volkswagen, is undergoing restructuring to address weak demand and high costs, said it would lower its future break-even point to fewer than 200,000 units, compared with total deliveries last year of 279,449. Porsche has already seen [USN:L8N3YH0HP TEXT:"deliveries slump"] by almost 10% globally since the year of its blockbuster listing in 2022, as plunging demand in China and tariff woes in the United States hit two of the brand's most important markets. During a capital markets day at the company's development centre in Weissach, CEO Michael Leiters will seek to assure investors that a focus on high-end sports cars like the 911 and luxury SUVs will put the carmaker back on track. Porsche set its long-term target for a group operating margin of 15% as part of the strategy. In the medium term, meaning roughly within five years, it is aiming for a range of 10% to 15%. Its profit margin collapsed last year to 1.1%, a fraction of the double-digit, Ferrari-style margins targeted when the Stuttgart-based carmaker went public four years ago under Oliver Blume, Leiters' predecessor. Blume remains CEO of Volkswagen, where he is [USN:L8N45M0TZ TEXT:"battling with unions"] to push through a [USN:L8N44W0B8 TEXT:"drastic overhaul"] of the German auto group, including some 100,000 layoffs worldwide and the closure of up to four German plants. Porsche, for its part, is cutting [USN:L8N43T10N TEXT:"9,000 positions"] by 2035, reducing its total workforce by a fifth, as job losses mount in the German automotive industry under pressure from low-cost Chinese rivals. Leiters is pursuing a "value over volume" strategy and [USN:L8N3ZZ09Q TEXT:"pivoting back"] to combustion-engine models after costly missteps on EVs under Blume. He also hopes to cut development costs by increasing platform-sharing with fellow Volkswagen brand Audi, the company said on Wednesday. "The ultimate goal is to further strengthen our unique sports car brand — across all model lines and with new, highly desirable models in particularly high-margin segments," CEO Michael Leiters said. "At the moment, the main focus is on reducing costs and making the company more financially robust."

item.title: Tesla is browbeating the EU to approve its ‘Full Self-Driving’ tech. The pressure is working.
item.description: Elon Musk’s EV company is running a social-media campaign blaming European traffic deaths on red tape. Its safety claims don’t hold up, experts say, but regulators are starting to buckle.
item.dc:creator: Chris Kirkham, Abhirup Roy, Marie Mannes
item.content:encoded: REUTERS/Jeremy Schultz/Illustration As Tesla chases an elusive prize – government approval of its “Full Self-Driving” technology across Europe – the US automaker is waging a pressure campaign casting safety regulators as feckless bureaucrats blocking its life-saving technology. Elon Musk's company has pushed regulators directly to reduce the rigor of safety reviews, submitted its own research making bold crash-reduction claims, and used social media to mobilize Tesla enthusiasts to demand speedy approvals. The strategy has worked so far, winning a critical first approval in the Netherlands that cleared the way for a Europe-wide vote expected soon by regulators from 27 European Union countries. Seven other EU countries, including the Czech Republic , Belgium and Denmark, have granted Tesla national approvals for the driver-assistance technology, which is not fully autonomous. But Tesla’s campaign is built on faulty company safety research that can’t support the company’s claims to officials or the public, according to seven traffic-safety researchers who examined its methodology for Reuters. The automaker sent the flawed studies broadly to European regulators seeking their support after it secured approval in the Netherlands. The Dutch evaluation had outsized importance because the EU’s process required first getting signoff from one member country that agrees to endorse the technology for EU-wide approval. Other countries’ regulators are now relying heavily on the Dutch research to decide their own votes. During that Netherlands review, Tesla repeatedly sought to scale back the intensity of the regulator’s examination, and it pushed – with some success – to set the terms and methods of its evaluation and testing, according to a Reuters review of correspondence between the automaker and the regulator, which has not been previously reported. Dutch staffers often responded with conciliatory notes emphasizing the regulator’s desire to collaborate with Tesla on “shared” or “mutual” objectives, raising concerns about its impartiality among five autonomous-vehicle regulation experts who reviewed the exchanges for Reuters. Tesla did not respond to detailed questions from Reuters on its safety research and interactions with European regulators. RDW, the regulator responsible for vehicle safety in the Netherlands, didn’t comment on its correspondence with Tesla or the company’s European data. In a statement, RDW said it “assesses driver assistance systems from all manufacturers objectively and independently.” It added that engagement with a manufacturer “is a routine part of the assessment process and does not compromise the independence or thoroughness of our assessment.” For this report on Tesla’s European pressure campaign, Reuters obtained hundreds of pages of email correspondence between Tesla and regulators in the Netherlands, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Estonia, Italy and Switzerland; reviewed safety studies Tesla distributed to regulators across Europe; and interviewed seven traffic-safety researchers who examined Tesla’s crash-reduction claims. Together, the documents and interviews provide the first detailed account of how Tesla sought to influence the Dutch review of FSD and used flawed claims about the technology’s life-saving potential to press regulators across Europe. Tesla produced an “evidence dashboard” on Full Self-Driving (FSD) safety that it said it shared with EU member-state regulators in April. The company’s Europe-specific research compares FSD-equipped Tesla cars driven by its own professional engineering drivers to all Tesla cars driven by ordinary owners across Europe. But it couldn’t determine relative crash rates because its sample of miles driven in FSD-piloted vehicles was too small – in the tens or hundreds of thousands – to meaningfully compare to the hundreds of millions of miles covered by manually driven Teslas in Europe, according to the seven traffic-safety researchers’ review of company research. Instead, Tesla used a set of driving behaviors as “surrogates” for measuring crashes – horn honking, low blinker-usage frequency, rapid acceleration or deceleration, automatic emergency braking and hard cornering. The company says it can track such maneuvers through its in-car technology, but it hasn’t sought outside peer review of its data or its methodology for analyzing it. The traffic safety researchers told Reuters that some of these driving behaviors, such as honking and blinker usage, are poor indicators of crash danger. Others, like hard braking, can be better proxies. But they have their own limitations, the researchers said, and their relation to crash rates isn’t well-established. All of the researchers said Tesla’s study provides no evidence of the central claim in the company’s European lobbying campaign – that FSD prevents fatal crashes. The researchers also questioned Tesla’s use of professional engineering drivers as a comparison. Trained drivers are more familiar with how FSD works and when and how they might need to intervene to prevent crashes or avoid the specific driving behaviors Tesla tracked. Tesla calls the system “Full Self-Driving” but adds “(Supervised)” because it requires a human driver's full attention. The automaker warns drivers to pay strict attention and stay ready to take over if FSD fails – transitions that autonomous-driving experts say can be difficult and dangerous. In its Europe study, Tesla says the professional drivers’ intimate familiarity with FSD makes its data collection more accurate because they rarely turn the system off. In the Europe study’s fine print, Tesla warns that its comparisons of FSD driving and human driving behaviors can’t be interpreted as “causal estimates,” an acknowledgment that FSD’s performance on those measures won’t necessarily translate to lower crash rates. But Tesla and Musk don’t disclose the research’s limitations in their social-media posts blaming European regulators for traffic deaths. When French transportation minister Philippe Tabarot said in July that his country couldn’t support EU-wide expansion of FSD due to safety concerns, Musk posted on his social media platform X that “delaying the approval of FSD in France will cost lives.” Musk responded to a video featuring French Transportation Minister Philippe Tabarot by claiming Paris’ stance would endanger public safety. Such claims go far beyond what Tesla’s research can support, said Marco Benedetti, an assistant research scientist at the University of Michigan Transportation Research Institute and a former statistician at the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). “When you start getting into ‘lives saved,’ that’s where it gets nonsensical,” he said. TESLA’S LONG HISTORY OF EXAGGERATED SAFETY CLAIMS Tesla’s inflated safety claims to European regulators are the latest in a long history of company exaggerations involving FSD’s safety and readiness for fully autonomous driving. The automaker has for years faced US federal investigations and lawsuits over crashes and deaths blamed on its FSD or Autopilot driver-assistance systems. Every year for a decade, chief executive Musk has asserted Tesla would deliver fully autonomous vehicles no later than the following year. After launching a small robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, in June 2025, Musk promised “hyperexponential” growth of a technology Tesla says can work anywhere on earth. Instead, Tesla has expanded robotaxis slowly in Austin and a handful of areas in Texas and Florida. The bulk of Tesla’s $1.5 trillion stock-market value is tied to investors’ belief that it will dominate self-driving technology globally. A Reuters investigation found the automaker is nowhere close to deploying self-driving cars safely at scale and that it used unsound statistical methodology to claim FSD is already up to 10 times safer than a human driver. The automaker, for instance, relied on an apples-and-oranges comparison of crashes in FSD-piloted Teslas with all crashes nationally. For Teslas using FSD, the company counted only crashes with airbag deployments; it then compared that rate with all crashes in federal data where a tow truck removed a vehicle – a criterion that includes a far higher number of less serious crashes. Tesla submitted the same misleading US research to European regulators, along with its more recent Europe-specific study. When you start getting into ‘lives saved,’ that’s where it gets nonsensical. Marco Benedetti, an assistant research scientist at the University of Michigan Transportation Research Institute Some of the traffic-safety researchers interviewed by Reuters said Tesla’s European study marked an improvement over its US research and included more disclosures acknowledging shortcomings of its methodology. Further, they said, making safety comparisons of a system like FSD to a human driver are inherently difficult. That’s in part because human drivers still play a critical role in operating FSD safely, making it difficult to attribute any perceived benefit solely to FSD. Human drivers can also turn the system on and off, and tend to avoid using it in complex driving situations they perceive to be dangerous, the researchers said. The main problem, all of the researchers said, is that Tesla makes exaggerated public safety claims that go far beyond what its research proves in both the US and Europe. Daniel McGehee, an engineering professor and director of the University of Iowa's Driving Safety Research Institute, said Tesla’s European study presents "potentially useful evidence of system performance" but stops well short of showing FSD saves lives. Tesla enthusiast Kees Roelandschap drove around Amsterdam hands-free with his electric car in April, several days after Dutch regulators approved the use of Tesla's driver-assistance software. REUTERS/Bart Biesemans FSD approval is critical to Tesla’s ambitions in Europe, where the company is only now regaining market share after steep sales declines stemming from rising electric-vehicle competition and consumer backlash over Musk’s backing of US President Donald Trump and far-right European politicians. Tesla now competes with dozens of new EVs from European brands and from surging Chinese EV makers, many of which offer FSD-like driver-assistance technology in their home market. FSD is currently available in the United States, where it didn’t need regulatory approval, along with the European countries that recently approved it and a handful of others, including Canada, Mexico, Australia and South Korea. The automaker has struggled for years to secure approval in China, its second-biggest market behind the US. Tesla would be the first automaker to win EU approval for an advanced driver-assistance system allowing hands-free operation on any road. Currently, regulations only allow hands-free systems on highways. In the EU-wide vote, Tesla needs support from regulators in 55% of EU-member countries constituting 65% of the region’s population. REGULATOR’S ‘SHARED GOALS AND OBJECTIVES’ WITH TESLA Staffers of the Dutch regulator, RDW, eased aspects of its FSD safety evaluation in response to repeated complaints from Tesla as it reviewed the system starting in 2024, correspondence between the company and the regulator shows. RDW ultimately found FSD could improve safety if used correctly and recommended EU-wide approval. The exchanges, which have not been previously reported, raise concerns over whether Tesla exerted undue influence over the safety review of its own technology, according to autonomous-vehicle regulation experts who reviewed the correspondence for Reuters. Throughout the process, Tesla representatives asserted the company should have shared decision-making power in how the review would be conducted. Staffers for the regulator, in turn, often assured Tesla of their desire to work collaboratively toward mutual goals. In this email to Tesla, obtained by Reuters, Dutch regulator RDW said it was willing to 'adjust or reduce' the intensity of a regulatory review. In November 2024, early in Tesla's discussions with RDW, the company pushed the regulator to start testing vehicles by month’s end. When a regulator responded with a commitment to deliver Tesla a project plan by then, a responding Tesla staffer reiterated the demand for immediate testing. “Keep in mind that this is mission critical for our leadership,” the Tesla representative wrote. “Our leadership will measure the goodwill to do this project with RDW by this ‘test start’ milestone.” The start of testing took longer. But Tesla won concessions from Dutch regulators after complaining about the costs, methods and time needed for other aspects of the review, according to the exchanges between the company and RDW. Unlike in the US, automakers in Europe must pay regulators’ expenses for evaluation of new-vehicle models, systems or parts. The costs disputed by Tesla ranged from tens to hundreds of thousands of euros, small sums relative to the $95 billion in revenue posted last year by the world’s most valuable automaker. Tesla objected, for instance, to paying for five RDW staffers to travel to a May 2025 meeting at Tesla’s Gigafactory in Berlin. The company said it expected only two to three staffers and argued most conversations should be held remotely. RDW responded that only two staff members' expenses would be billed to Tesla and others might not attend. In an April 2025 email to RDW, a Tesla employee balked at RDW’s breakdown of €365,000 in costs for testing permits, technical work and other services RDW conducted over a five-month period ending in March 2025. The automaker complained of the “extremely high cost” and said it would withhold payment until it received a "granular" accounting of RDW's operations, including credentials, hours worked and hourly cost of every RDW employee assigned to the project. An RDW staffer offered to dial back the review’s intensity a week later, inviting Tesla to “share any suggestions on how we might adjust or reduce the required effort moving forward.” RDW redacted all the names of Tesla and RDW staffers, along with large portions of their correspondence, before providing the documents to Reuters. The extent of the regulator’s redactions, where entire emails or large parts of exchanges are obscured, leaves substantial gaps in the dealings between Tesla and RDW. Bryant Walker Smith, a University of South Carolina law professor focused on autonomous-driving regulation, questioned whether Tesla was challenging relatively inconsequential expenses as a way to reduce regulatory scrutiny. "These don't seem like huge amounts,” he said. "My immediate concern was: Is reducing costs a proxy for reducing oversight?" In December 2024, Tesla complained that travel logistics for an RDW inspector to “witness” certain tests were wasting valuable time and that test reports submitted by Tesla should suffice. RDW responded by proposing to monitor part of the tests remotely. The type of test being performed was unclear in the documents because portions of them were redacted by RDW. In a January 2025 email, Tesla questioned RDW’s request for a meeting to discuss Tesla’s remote software system, or over-the-air (OTA) updates, and instead offered a written summary. The automaker and the regulator could "decide together if an OTA scrutiny meeting is justified,” a Tesla employee wrote. An RDW staffer, in a partially redacted email, assured Tesla that the regulator didn’t want to “dive too deep in technical details,” and didn’t “question the quality and process for OTA’s.” 'It was not my intention to dive too deep in technical details': A redacted January 2025 email from an RDW staffer to Tesla. In an April 2025 email to RDW, Tesla said some tests that the regulator had conducted in Lelystad, Netherlands, “should have been handled in a different way” and demanded that RDW get written approval before certain tests of FSD on its vehicles. Tesla also told RDW it needed to tell the company in advance exactly what kinds of tests it would conduct and provide a list of names and roles of its safety drivers and passengers performing them. RDW responded two days later and agreed to provide the names, after getting sign-off from the drivers, and highlighted its "shared goals and objectives" with Tesla. An RDW staffer wrote: "We hope you recognize that our efforts are driven by the best intentions to support and achieve those mutual aims." 'Our efforts are driven by the best intentions': An April 2025 email from RDW to Tesla. The regulator’s redactions appear to obscure the type of testing it was discussing with Tesla. RDW has shared data on its FSD testing with other European regulators but declined to release it publicly . Both Tesla and RDW argue such information would reveal Tesla trade secrets, the correspondence between them shows. Some transportation regulation experts disagree. RDW's accommodation of some Tesla demands conflicts with the role of a regulatory watchdog seeking to protect public safety, said Nynke Vellinga, a senior researcher at University of Groningen in the Netherlands, who specializes in legal aspects of autonomous driving. "An authority like the RDW needs to be very strong in saying: No, this is what we deem necessary,” she said. “And if we cannot do it, that means that you're not getting approval." The regulator RDW told Reuters that it conducted an “extensive independent investigation,” which included testing on closed tracks and public roads, in various conditions. RDW declined to specify how it measured safety performance during such testing. Five of the regulators from the seven other EU countries that have approved FSD so far – Denmark, Belgium, Croatia, Estonia and Slovenia – declined to comment or did not respond to questions about Tesla’s safety research, its social-media pressure campaign and exchanges between Tesla and RDW provided by Reuters. Officials in Lithuania and the Czech Republic said the company’s social media claims did not influence their assessment of its technology. The Czech regulator added that it has no reason to question RDW’s impartiality. RIDICULING REGULATORS, FIRING UP THE FAN BASE At Tesla’s annual shareholder meeting last November, Musk mocked European regulators, describing “crazy conversations” with them that he said were “like a Franz Kafka novel.” “People’s lives are at stake here,” he said. “So definitely, pressure from our customers in Europe to push the regulators to approve would be appreciated.” Boasts about life-saving technology were a key feature of the misleading US safety research that Musk and other Tesla leaders regularly touted last year as the company’s board successfully sold investors on approving a compensation package awarding Musk up to $1 trillion in Tesla stock. The company leaders regularly cited the claim in its US research that FSD-piloted Teslas are 10 times safer than the typical US vehicle. The company later revised the research and downgraded the claim to seven times safer. The company created a US-focused safety website saying FSD could save more than 32,000 lives and prevent more than 1.9 million injuries annually. Traffic-safety researchers who reviewed Tesla’s safety research and statistics for Reuters called those figures essentially meaningless. That’s because they were based on the unrealistic assumption that every US vehicle would be replaced by an FSD-enabled Tesla – and that every vehicle was, in fact, far safer than the one it replaced, as Tesla inaccurately contended. Tesla has made similarly misleading claims in Europe, mischaracterizing its own research, according to experts who reviewed its methodology. Last month, Tesla said on X it had decided to “open-source” the European safety study it said it had given months earlier to European regulators. Tesla called its study “one of the key pieces of evidence used to support the Netherlands approval.” In this September 2026 post on X, Tesla alleged FSD's safety benefits are “locked behind bureaucracy." In posting the safety research, which doesn’t address fatalities, Tesla said that an average of 53 road deaths per day in Europe are “largely preventable with technology we have today.” “Yet in much of Europe,” Tesla said, “that safety benefit remains locked behind bureaucracy.” Tesla supporters across Europe have used the same rhetoric in angry posts on X blaming regulators for traffic deaths. After Musk accused French transportation minister Tabarot of endangering lives in July, Tesla enthusiasts pounced on Tabarot’s X account. One user said that FSD would have kept him safe recently as he was tired driving home from work and drifting in his lane. “YOU put me – and other road users along my route – in danger!” the post said, in French. “From now on, YOU are RESPONSIBLE for accidents and deaths on the road.” Another user, replying to Tabarot’s account, wrote: “Your name will not be forgotten. Every death this technology can prevent will be laid at your door.” Correspondence obtained by Reuters through public-records requests shows that officials in Sweden and Norway have received dozens of emails and messages from Tesla enthusiasts citing claims about FSD’s life-saving capabilities. Other European governments denied or haven’t responded to Reuters requests seeking communications on FSD received from the public. One August 2025 email to Swedish road regulators from a Tesla Model 3 owner said: “Not approving this means that more people die unnecessarily” and asked why regulators hadn’t approved FSD “when the statistics are so clear.” A group of Norwegian Tesla owners in May this year wrote an email to Norwegian regulators criticizing what they called “the passive and bureaucratic way” officials there handled deliberations over FSD, “instead of showing the necessary leadership and acting quickly to save lives.” Stein-Helge Mundal, a chief engineer at the Norwegian Public Roads Administration, wrote in a November 2025 email to counterparts in Sweden, Finland and Denmark that Tesla was “advising their customers to contact RDW and their national authorities,” after a Tesla account on X urged customers to contact European regulators and linked to a contact form for Dutch regulator RDW. Social posts calling for EU regulators to approve FSD. Mundal wrote to fellow regulators that, in light of Tesla’s “pressure” strategy, “we will need to use a lot of effort to answer misled consumers.” In a statement to Reuters, Mundal said: “We do not approve systems because they are popular, and we do not reject them because they are controversial.” He added that the term “Full Self-Driving” could lead drivers to assume the system “can do more than it actually can.” Norwegian regulators consider statements about lives saved to be “marketing claims,” he said. We will need to use a lot of effort to answer misled consumers. Stein-Helge Mundal, a chief engineer at the Norwegian Public Roads Administration Hans Nordin, an investigator at the Swedish Transport Agency, declined to comment on Tesla’s pressure campaign or the safety data it presented. Denmark has approved FSD. Sweden and Finland haven’t announced a decision. In France, minister Tabarot signaled a change of heart last month. He posted a photo of himself in a virtual meeting with a smiling Musk, describing a “constructive exchange” about FSD. He described “working closely” with Tesla on changes “that will enable France to support its approval.” In a statement to Reuters, the French transportation ministry didn’t respond to the criticism from Musk and other X users, or explain what led to Tabarot’s more optimistic tone.

item.title: Vance dice que Irán debe reducir su capacidad de enriquecimiento para poner fin a la guerra
item.description: JD Vance dijo en una entrevista exclusiva con Reuters que Irán debe reducir de forma "significativa" su capacidad de enriquecimiento nuclear para satisfacer las exigencias estadounidenses y poner fin a la guerra de siete meses entre ambos países, aunque Washington no tiene claro cómo toma Teherán las decisiones en las negociaciones.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage
item.content:encoded: JD Vance dijo en una entrevista exclusiva con Reuters que Irán debe reducir de forma "significativa" su capacidad de enriquecimiento nuclear para satisfacer las exigencias estadounidenses y poner fin a la guerra de siete meses entre ambos países, aunque Washington no tiene claro cómo toma Teherán las decisiones en las negociaciones. El vicepresidente de Estados Unidos, que desde hace tiempo se muestra escéptico sobre la participación de Estados Unidos en guerras en el extranjero, ha asumido un papel destacado en las negociaciones para resolver el conflicto y medió en junio en un acuerdo de paz provisional que pronto se vino abajo. La guerra ha sacudido los mercados energéticos mundiales y se ha convertido en un lastre político para el presidente Donald Trump y sus correligionarios republicanos de cara a las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato de noviembre. Vance dijo el lunes, tras un viaje de campaña a Alaska, que cualquier acuerdo exigiría que Irán redujera su capacidad de enriquecimiento nuclear, en lugar de ofrecer garantías de futuras reducciones de su programa nuclear. "Si no quieren un arma nuclear, ¿para qué necesitan combustible enriquecido al 60%? Y si quieren demostrar su compromiso de no fabricar un arma nuclear, no produzcan combustible altamente enriquecido. Ese es un requisito mínimo básico", dijo Vance. "Creo que, si quieren demostrar su compromiso de no fabricar un arma nuclear, tomarían alguna medida significativa para reducir su capacidad de enriquecimiento". Irán y Estados Unidos han intercambiado propuestas en las últimas semanas para poner fin a la guerra y reabrir el estrecho de Ormuz, una ruta vital para el transporte marítimo de energía a escala mundial. Trump rechazó la última oferta de Teherán y ha advertido de que las operaciones militares podrían intensificarse después de las elecciones de mitad de mandato. Vance dijo que Estados Unidos seguía abierto a un acuerdo, pero exigiría concesiones concretas de Irán en materia nuclear. "No vamos a cambiar palabras por acciones", dijo Vance. NO ESTÁ CLARO CÓMO TOMA IRÁN LAS DECISIONES, DICE VANCE Vance dijo que Washington no tiene claro quién toma las decisiones en Teherán, una situación que complica aún más el escenario. El vicepresidente afirmó que Estados Unidos mantenía conversaciones con el presidente iraní, Masud Pezeshkian, y el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores, Abás Araqchi. Sin embargo, dijo que no estaba claro cuánto poder tienen dentro de la estructura de poder iraní, después de que los ataques conjuntos de Estados Unidos e Israel al inicio de la guerra mataran al líder supremo, el ayatolá Alí Jamenei. "Una de las cosas que hemos observado es que no está del todo claro cómo se toman las decisiones en su país", dijo Vance. Por su parte, Trump afirmó el martes que su "mayor problema" es que nadie sabe quién dirige Irán. El portavoz del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores iraní dijo el domingo que los funcionarios estadounidenses saben perfectamente quiénes son sus interlocutores iraníes y cómo funciona el sistema de toma de decisiones de Irán. "El problema es precisamente el contrario: radica en las posturas contradictorias y los mensajes dispares de los funcionarios estadounidenses", dijo Esmail Baghaei en una rueda de prensa semanal. Vance dijo a Reuters que ha mantenido conversaciones personales con comandantes sobre el terreno para evaluar las condiciones en el campo de batalla. Desestimó las preocupaciones por la escasez de municiones esenciales y añadió que, aunque las tropas iraníes pueden atacar periódicamente buques mercantes en el estrecho de Ormuz, en gran medida son incapaces de impedir las exportaciones de energía a través de esa vía marítima. Vance declinó decir si encabezaba las conversaciones de paz, aunque a menudo se lo señala como el principal negociador de la Casa Blanca. "Desde luego que estamos involucrados", dijo. "En última instancia, quien lleva las riendas es el presidente de Estados Unidos". La guerra —y su costo mensual de 3.000 millones de dólares— se ha convertido en uno de los temas centrales de la campaña electoral. El encarecimiento de la energía ha puesto a Trump y a los republicanos a la defensiva en los estados donde la contienda está reñida y que decidirán el control del Congreso. Vance ha tratado de moderar las críticas a la gestión del conflicto por parte de Trump, al decir a los votantes que no deberían dejar que ese asunto les impida apoyar a los republicanos en las elecciones del próximo mes. En Alaska, Vance participó en un mitin en apoyo del senador republicano Dan Sullivan, que libra una reñida batalla por la reelección frente a su rival demócrata, Mary Peltola. Trump ganó en Alaska por 13 puntos porcentuales en 2024, pero el aumento del costo de la vida ha convertido al estado en un escenario de disputa electoral. Antes de hablar con Reuters, Vance centró buena parte de su discurso en las dificultades para afrontar los gastos cotidianos, especialmente los energéticos. La ubicación remota de Alaska encarece los bienes de consumo, y la producción de energía es una industria clave. Los asistentes al mitin estallaron en vítores cuando Sullivan estuvo a punto de presentar a Vance como presidente de Estados Unidos, en lugar de vicepresidente. Vance es considerado uno de los principales aspirantes republicanos a suceder a Trump en la Casa Blanca. Vance dijo después a Reuters que no había decidido si se presentaría a las elecciones presidenciales de 2028. "Soy de los que dejan las cosas para después por naturaleza", dijo. "La verdad es que no lo he pensado mucho".

item.title: India sube las tasas de interés por primera vez en casi cuatro años
item.description: El banco central de India subió el miércoles su tasa de interés de referencia para las operaciones de recompra en 25 puntos básicos, hasta el 5,5%, lo que supone la primera subida en casi cuatro años en un contexto de inflación creciente y fuerte crecimiento económico.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Kalra, Abinaya V
item.content:encoded: El banco central de India subió el miércoles su tasa de interés de referencia para las operaciones de recompra (INREPO=ECI) en 25 puntos básicos, hasta el 5,5%, lo que supone la primera subida en casi cuatro años en un contexto de inflación creciente y fuerte crecimiento económico. El banco central también anticipó nuevas subidas de tasas al cambiar su postura de "neutral" a "endurecimiento calibrado", aunque el gobernador Sanjay Malhotra dijo que el alcance y el momento de cualquier otra subida dependerán de los resultados reales de la inflación y el crecimiento. India se ha sumado a los principales bancos centrales en la subida de las tasas, ya que el aumento de los precios del petróleo provocado por la guerra en Irán alimenta la inflación, reduce el poder adquisitivo y lastra las divisas. Las escasas lluvias monzónicas, relacionadas con El Niño, han agravado las presiones sobre los precios en la tercera economía más grande de Asia. El comité de tasas, compuesto por seis miembros, votó por unanimidad a favor de la subida de tasas. Casi el 60% de los economistas encuestados por Reuters esperaba un aumento de 25 puntos básicos en la tasa repo. "Está claro que las perspectivas de inflación ya no son favorables", dijo Malhotra en su discurso sobre política monetaria. "Existen indicios de unas expectativas de inflación elevadas y de una generalización de las presiones sobre los precios", añadió. El rendimiento del bono de referencia indio a 10 años se disparaba hasta el 7,2655%, 5 puntos básicos por encima tras la decisión del RBI, mientras que el tipo de cambio de la rupia seguía prácticamente sin cambios en torno a 96,36. El índice bursátil de referencia Nifty 50 y el BSE Sensex bajaban un 0,6% y un 0,7%, respectivamente. El RBI prevé una inflación del 5,2%, lo que supone un ligero aumento con respecto a su previsión anterior del 5%. La inflación subyacente se sitúa en el 4,4%, frente al 4,3% anterior. La inflación al consumo se aceleró en agosto hasta el 4,82% respecto al año anterior, situándose por encima del objetivo a medio plazo del 4% del Banco de la Reserva de India por tercer mes consecutivo. El aumento de los precios del combustible y los alimentos está afectando ahora a toda la economía, ya que casi la mitad de la cesta de la compra registra una inflación superior al 4%. Al mismo tiempo, el crecimiento económico se mantiene sólido, lo que da al banco central un mayor margen de maniobra para aumentar el coste de los préstamos para consumidores y empresas. El banco central prevé que el crecimiento del PIB en el actual ejercicio fiscal se sitúe en el 7,1%, 40 puntos básicos por encima de sus previsiones anteriores. El crecimiento del PIB en el trimestre de abril a junio se situó en el 7,8%, muy por encima de la previsión del banco central, que era del 7%.

item.title: Bruselas estudia gravar a las tecnológicas con un impuesto a grandes corporaciones, según el FT
item.description: Bruselas está barajando la posibilidad de gravar a las grandes empresas tecnológicas estadounidenses mediante un impuesto general sobre las grandes corporaciones, como parte de su intento por aumentar los ingresos de la UE y evitar al mismo tiempo una reacción negativa por parte del Gobierno de Trump, según informó el miércoles el Financial Times.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bruselas está barajando la posibilidad de gravar a las grandes empresas tecnológicas estadounidenses mediante un impuesto general sobre las grandes corporaciones, como parte de su intento por aumentar los ingresos de la UE y evitar al mismo tiempo una reacción negativa por parte del Gobierno de Trump, según informó el miércoles el Financial Times. La Comisión Europea estaba trabajando en nuevas formas de obtener más ingresos de grupos tecnológicos como Apple (AAPL.O) , Meta (META.O) y Google (GOOGL.O) sin señalarlos específicamente, dijo el periódico, que cita a seis funcionarios con conocimiento de las conversaciones. Bruselas estaba barajando cambios en su propuesta "Corporate Resource for Europe" (CORE), que obligaría a todas las empresas que operan en la UE con unos ingresos superiores a 100 millones de euros (112,32 millones de dólares) al año a pagar una contribución fiscal anual a tanto alzado, según el reporte. En su forma actual, la CORE exige a estas empresas el pago de una cuota anual fija de entre 100.000 y 750.000 euros, lo que supone solo una pequeña parte de los beneficios de una empresa multinacional. "Algunas capitales (de la UE) se oponen a un impuesto digital puro porque no quieren molestar a los estadounidenses, y muchas más se oponen a la propuesta CORE", dijo un funcionario de la UE al FT. "La solución es ampliar (el impuesto) para que abarque prácticamente a todas las grandes empresas". Reuters no pudo verificar de inmediato esta información. La Comisión Europea, la Asociación de la Industria Informática y de las Comunicaciones (CCIA, por sus siglas en inglés), que representa a varias empresas tecnológicas estadounidenses, Apple, Google y Meta no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios de Reuters fuera del horario laboral habitual. El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, amenazó en junio con aplicar un arancel del 100% a todos los productos procedentes de cualquier país que establezca un impuesto sobre los servicios digitales de empresas estadounidenses. La oficina del representante de Comercio de EEUU, que lleva tiempo amenazando a los países europeos con aranceles de represalia si se implementan dichos impuestos, ha argumentado que estos gravámenes discriminan a las empresas estadounidenses, que dominan el sector a nivel mundial. (1 dólar = 0,8903 euros)

item.title: Equinor says trading profit will top guidance in third quarter
item.description: Equinor's downstream division, which includes energy trading, will report a third-quarter result that exceeds the company's guidance of $400 million, the Norwegian energy group said on Wednesday.

item.title: Football–Messi fait ses adieux à l'équipe d'Argentine
item.description: Lionel Messi a donné mardi une dernière leçon de maître sous le maillot bleu et blanc, le capitaine de l'équipe de football d'Argentine ayant mis un point d'orgue à sa carrière internationale de 21 ans en marquant un but lors d'un match amical contre le Bénin.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lionel Messi a donné mardi une dernière leçon de maître sous le maillot bleu et blanc, le capitaine de l'équipe de football d'Argentine ayant mis un point d'orgue à sa carrière internationale de 21 ans en marquant un but lors d'un match amical contre le Bénin. Les adieux du joueur de 39 ans devant plus de 85.000 supporters dans un stade Monumental comble ont été moins une affaire de football qu'une véritable célébration rendant hommage au dévouement de Lionel Messi envers l'équipe nationale. Les monuments de la capitale se sont mis aux couleurs emblématiques bleu ciel et blanc de l'équipe, tandis que des feux d'artifice ont illuminé le ciel au-dessus du stade bondé et que les supporters chantaient l'hymne national argentin. La famille de Lionel Messi assistait au spectacle depuis les tribunes, aux côtés de certains des champions du monde argentins de 1978, 1986 et 2022. Quelques heures plus tôt, un immense maillot orné de l'inscription "Merci" avait été déployé au Mémorial du drapeau national à Rosario, la ville natale de Lionel Messi. Alors que le car de l'équipe quittait le centre d'entraînement qui porte son nom, Lionel Messi a essuyé ses larmes devant les milliers de personnes massées le long du parcours. Lorsque les équipes sont entrées sur le terrain, le capitaine du Bénin a remis au numéro 10 argentin un cadeau et une lettre lors de la poignée de main d'avant-match. Après une première mi-temps sans but, Lionel Messi a délivré la passe décisive à Nicolas Otamendi, qui a ouvert le score pour l'Argentine. Nicolas Otamendi, qui a partagé 17 ans de carrière avec Messi en équipe nationale, dont quatre Coupes du monde, et mettait lui aussi un terme à sa carrière internationale. Lionel Messi a ensuite servi Nico Paz, qui a inscrit le deuxième but. Lionel Messi a terminé en transformant un penalty, inscrivant ainsi son 126e but en sélection et portant le score de la rencontre à 3-0. Au coup de sifflet final, coéquipiers, adversaires et arbitre se sont rassemblés autour de Lionel Messi pour l'étreindre, avant qu'un spectacle de drones n'illumine le ciel pour marquer la fin de sa carrière en équipe d'Argentine. Lionel Messi quitte la sélection en tant que joueur le plus capé de l'Argentine (208 sélections) et meilleur buteur de l'histoire.

item.title: Israel conmemora el tercer aniversario del ataque de Hamás, desencadenante de la ofensiva en Gaza
item.description: Los israelíes conmemorarán este miércoles el tercer aniversario del ataque de Hamás contra Israel el 7 de octubre de 2023, que desencadenó una ofensiva militar que destruyó gran parte de Gaza, donde las condiciones siguen siendo desesperadas a pesar del alto el fuego, en vigor desde hace un año, que tiene como objetivo poner fin a la guerra de forma definitiva.
item.dc:creator: Steven Scheer
item.content:encoded: Los israelíes conmemorarán este miércoles el tercer aniversario del ataque de Hamás contra Israel el 7 de octubre de 2023, que desencadenó una ofensiva militar que destruyó gran parte de Gaza, donde las condiciones siguen siendo desesperadas a pesar del alto el fuego, en vigor desde hace un año, que tiene como objetivo poner fin a la guerra de forma definitiva. Los ataques, durante los cuales los milicianos mataron a 1.200 personas y se llevaron a 251 rehenes a Gaza, marcaron el día más mortífero de la historia de Israel. Los posteriores bombardeos y operaciones terrestres de Israel han causado la muerte de más de 74.000 personas en Gaza, según las autoridades sanitarias de la zona. El miércoles, los israelíes celebrarán una vigilia en el recinto del festival de música Nova, cerca de la frontera con Gaza, donde 348 jóvenes fueron asesinados por los milicianos durante el ataque. También celebrarán un acto conmemorativo del aniversario en la Plaza de los Rehenes, en Tel Aviv. FALTAN 20 DÍAS PARA LAS ELECCIONES EN ISRAEL Este es el primer aniversario que los israelíes celebran sin ningún rehén retenido en Gaza, ya que tanto los fallecidos como los supervivientes fueron intercambiados con Hamás a cambio de palestinos encarcelados en prisiones israelíes. Los restos mortales del último rehén israelí se recuperaron en enero. Además, llega apenas 20 días antes de las primeras elecciones en Israel desde el ataque, unos comicios que se consideran un referéndum sobre el largo mandato del primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu. Netanyahu ha rechazado cualquier responsabilidad por la brecha de seguridad y se ha resistido a las peticiones de una investigación independiente. Esto ha frustrado a muchos en Israel, incluidas las familias de los fallecidos en los ataques, algunas de las cuales se han sumado a la carrera electoral. Una encuesta del Instituto para la Democracia de Israel reveló que el 68% de los israelíes judíos afirmaba que los acontecimientos del 7 de octubre eran un factor muy importante o bastante importante a la hora de decidir a qué partido votar. Las encuestas electorales indican que ni Netanyahu ni sus principales rivales obtendrían suficientes escaños en el Parlamento para formar una coalición si las elecciones se celebraran hoy. EL ALTO EL FUEGO DE EEUU NO DETIENE LOS ATAQUES ISRAELÍES NI DESARMA A HAMÁS Este aniversario es también el primero desde el acuerdo de alto el fuego del 10 de octubre de 2025, negociado por Estados Unidos, que puso fin a los principales combates, pero que no ha logrado detener los ataques israelíes en Gaza ni garantizar el desarme de Hamás y otros grupos milicianos. El acuerdo dejó a Israel al mando de alrededor del 53% de Gaza, territorio que las fuerzas israelíes han ampliado desde entonces hasta casi dos tercios. Hamás controla el tercio restante, donde los dos millones de habitantes viven en su mayoría en tiendas de campaña improvisadas y edificios bombardeados. La denominada "Junta de Paz" del presidente de EEUU, Donald Trump, ha propuesto varios planes para la reconstrucción de Gaza. Sin embargo, esos planes, que no tienen en cuenta los derechos de propiedad de los palestinos cuyas viviendas fueron destruidas, no han logrado el apoyo ni de Israel ni de Hamás, que siguen en un punto muerto en las negociaciones de alto el fuego. Ambas partes aún no se han puesto de acuerdo sobre los términos de un acuerdo que llevaría a Hamás a deponer las armas a cambio de la retirada de los efectivos israelíes. Israel dice que no se retirará hasta que Hamás se desarme por completo; Hamás afirma que ha aceptado un proceso por fases, pero que no se desarmará mientras continúen los ataques israelíes. Israel ha continuado una campaña de bombardeos en Gaza que ha causado la muerte de varios milicianos de Hamás en los últimos meses, pero que también ha acabado con la vida de muchos civiles, según las autoridades sanitarias de Gaza, cuyas cifras de fallecidos no distinguen entre civiles y combatientes. Más de 1.400 palestinos han perdido la vida en Gaza desde el alto el fuego de octubre de 2025, según las autoridades sanitarias. Durante el mismo periodo, cinco soldados israelíes han fallecido a manos de milicianos o en combate, según el ejército.

item.content:encoded: Das mit chronischen Finanzproblemen kämpfende deutsche Gesundheitswesen kann einer Studie zufolge durch einen stärkeren Einsatz von Digitalisierung und Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) stark entlastet werden. Jährlich ließen sich damit rund 80 Milliarden Euro zusätzlich erschließen, geht aus einer Analyse der Unternehmensberatung McKinsey hervor. Diese lag der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters am Mittwoch vorab vor. Demnach werden bereits jetzt 11,5 Milliarden Euro pro Jahr durch digitale Anwendungen wie das E-Rezept oder die elektronische Patientenakte realisiert - achtmal so viel wie 2022. "Die Fortschritte zeigen, dass Digitalisierung ein entscheidender Schlüssel sein kann, um dem Fachkräftemangel, steigenden Kosten und dem wachsenden Versorgungsbedarf im Gesundheitswesen zu begegnen", erklärte Katharina Sickmüller, Partnerin bei McKinsey und Co-Autorin der Studie. Das noch ungenutzte Potenzial entspreche rund 17 Prozent der relevanten Gesundheitsausgaben von 479 Milliarden Euro. Allein auf KI entfällt der Analyse zufolge ein Potenzial von 22,8 Milliarden Euro. Sie könne Fachkräfte von Routinetätigkeiten entlasten, die Steuerung von Personal und Behandlungen verbessern und die Dokumentation automatisieren. Konkret könnten etwa virtuelle Assistenten Gespräche in der Versorgung in Echtzeit dokumentieren und für die elektronische Patientenakte aufbereiten. KI-Systeme können demnach auch Abrechnungsfehler erkennen, klinische Informationen strukturieren sowie Betten, Personal und Behandlungsabläufe vorausschauend steuern. Das reduziere administrative Lasten und schaffe mehr Zeit für die unmittelbare Versorgung. "Künstliche Intelligenz eröffnet die nächste Stufe der Digitalisierung", sagte Co-Autorin Kristin Tuot. "Entscheidend ist, KI nicht als Zusatztool zu verstehen, sondern sie sinnvoll in die Abläufe der Versorgung zu integrieren." Entscheidend für die Zukunft sei jedoch nicht mehr nur der Zugang zu Technologien, sondern vor allem deren tatsächliche Nutzung. Dies zeige sich besonders bei der elektronischen Patientenakte (ePA). Sie stehe zwar einem Großteil der Bevölkerung zur Verfügung, werde im Alltag aber kaum genutzt. Eine konsequentere Nutzung der bereits vorhandenen Akten allein könne hier etwa 6,2 Milliarden Euro heben. Das Potenzial ergibt sich der Studie zufolge zu 64 Prozent aus Produktivitätssteigerungen und zu 36 Prozent aus einer geringeren Nachfrage nach medizinischen Leistungen. Letztere könne etwa durch eine digitale Vorsortierung von Patienten, die Fernüberwachung chronisch Kranker oder Prävention erreicht werden. Das Potenzial ist nicht mit einem reinen Einsparpotenzial gleichzusetzen. Profitieren würden vor allem die Leistungserbringer wie Kliniken und Praxen, auf die rund zwei Drittel des Gesamtpotenzials entfallen. Ein Drittel käme den Kostenträgern wie den Krankenkassen zugute, so McKinsey.

item.title: Thai flood damage estimated at $178 million, industry federation says
item.description: Thailand's industrial sector has suffered damages worth an estimated 6 billion baht ($178 million) from floods that have swept through parts of the country since last month, a Federation of Thai Industries official said on Wednesday.

item.content:encoded: Thailand's industrial sector has suffered damages worth an estimated 6 billion baht ($178 million) from floods that have swept through parts of the country since last month, a Federation of Thai Industries official said on Wednesday. Despite disruptions, automotive assembly plants currently have enough parts in stock to continue production until Oct 12, FTI Secretary-General Panitarn Pavarolavidya said in a briefing. item.title: Ukraine-La Russie lance des attaques contre Kyiv, deux morts
item.description: La Russie a mené tôt mercredi des frappes contre Kyiv, faisant deux morts et endommageant des bâtiments et des entrepôts, ont déclaré les autorités locales.

item.content:encoded: La Russie a mené tôt mercredi des frappes contre Kyiv, faisant deux morts et endommageant des bâtiments et des entrepôts, ont déclaré les autorités locales. Des explosions ont été entendues dans la ville, a rapporté un témoin. Un site industriel de la ville de Dnipro, dans le sud-est de l'Ukraine, a été endommagé par des frappes russes, a déclaré le gouverneur régional Oleksandr Hanja sur Telegram, sans donner plus de détails.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Deux missiles lancés par les Houthis, ont visé mercredi matin l'aéroport international du port d'Aden, dans le sud du Yémen, a indiqué le service de presse du département de la sécurité d'Aden, indiquant qu'aucune victime n'avait été signalée. Cette attaque intervient dans un contexte de reprise des combats, après des semaines d'avancées effectuées par les rebelles houthis le long de la côte yéménite de la mer Rouge et une contre-offensive du gouvernement soutenu par l'Arabie saoudite qui a permis de reprendre des zones situées autour du détroit stratégique de Bab al Mandab. L'aéroport d'Aden est la principale porte d'entrée internationale desservant les régions du Yémen échappant au contrôle des Houthis.

item.title: Padres come up with clutch efforts, beat Brewers to force Game 4
item.description: Jake Cronenworth hit a tie-breaking homer in the fifth inning and Michael King registered a six-out save as the San Diego Padres staved off elimination with a 4-3 victory over the visiting Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday night in Game 3 of the National League Division Series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jake Cronenworth hit a tie-breaking homer in the fifth inning and Michael King registered a six-out save as the San Diego Padres staved off elimination with a 4-3 victory over the visiting Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday night in Game 3 of the National League Division Series. Cronenworth led off the bottom of the fifth by jumping on a first-pitch sweeper by JoJo Romero (0-1) and sending it over the wall to give the Padres a 3-2 advantage. After Padres star closer Mason Miller went on the paternity list prior to the game, King was called on to protect a 4-3 lead two days after throwing 72 pitches as the Game 2 starter. The right-hander gave up one hit and walked two to record the save. "I made myself available on Sunday, confirmed it with (manager Craig) Stammen today," King said after the win. "I knew that there was a chance it was going to be late in the game because of Mason's wife, but six outs to end the game is six outs to end the game. I wasn't as crisp as I'd like to be, but I'm very happy for a Game 4." William Contreras went 3-for-4 with a walk and a homer and Christian Yelich snapped his 19-game postseason streak without an RBI for the Brewers. Yelich and Cooper Pratt each had two hits. Game 4 of the best-of-five series is Wednesday night in San Diego. "We used a lot of energy today, and we've got to bring that same energy tomorrow also. It's going to be another fight just like the first three games, and I don't think I expect anything different," Stammen said. "The resilience we showed today, the stick-to-itativeness, the keep bouncing back, all the adjectives you can use for that, this team showed it all year, and they showed it especially again tonight. We're going to have to do it again tomorrow." Contreras and Brice Turang walked against King with one out in the ninth before Yelich hit a bullet that short-hopped into the glove of Padres shortstop Xander Bogaerts, who touched second and threw to first for the game-ending double play. "We didn't get the big hit at the big time, but do you fault Yelly for hitting one 107 there and Bogaerts making a great play? They got a great team, and they played great defense tonight. They really did," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. The Brewers lost their 12th consecutive road playoff game. "I really enjoy them. I enjoy the road losses. They feel good. Does it wear on me?" Murphy quipped. "That's a great point to bring up. It's tough to win on the road in playoff situations obviously. We've done a pretty good job at home, I'd say, but you're right. It's never fun." Left-hander Yuki Matsui (1-0) was credited with the win after retiring three batters over the fifth and sixth innings. In the bottom of the sixth, Bogaerts singled with two outs against right-hander Antonio Senzatela. Left-hander DL Hall entered and threw a wild pitch to move Bogaerts to second. Pinch hitter Miguel Andujar hit a broken-bat bouncer to shortstop that went between the legs of a leaping Bogaerts. Shortstop Pratt seemed slightly distracted and his ensuing throw to first bounced in front of Jake Bauers and caromed away a few feet as Bogaerts came around to score. In the seventh, Contreras stroked a two-out single off Bradgley Rodriguez and Turang followed with a single. Yelich then delivered an RBI single to bring the Brewers within 4-3, his first RBI since Game 7 of the 2018 NL Championship against the Los Angeles Dodgers. Garrett Mitchell then struck out to end the inning. San Diego scored twice in the third against Brewers starter Dustin May, who allowed two runs, three hits, two walks and struck out three in three-plus innings. Samad Taylor stroked a leadoff single, stole second and was sacrificed to third by Cronenworth. Taylor scored when Fernando Tatis Jr. hit a tapper to shortstop and was thrown out at first. Jackson Merrill followed with a single and stole second before Manny Machado delivered a run-scoring single to give the Padres a 2-0 lead. The Brewers got on the board in the fourth when Contreras smacked a leadoff homer to left off Nick Pivetta. It was Contreras' second homer of the series. Milwaukee started the fifth with back-to-back singles by Pratt and Sal Frelick. Joey Ortiz then laid down a bunt to move the runners up. Jason Adam replaced Pivetta and induced Jackson Chourio to hit a fly ball to shallow left. Pratt beat Dustin Harris' throw to knot the score at 2. Pivetta gave up two runs and five hits over 4 1/3 innings. The right-hander struck out four and walked none. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kosovo-Le Parlement élit un nouveau président, évite des élections anticipées
item.description: Le Parlement du Kosovo a élu l'économiste Justina Shiroka Pula à la présidence du pays, une fonction essentiellement honorifique, juste avant l'expiration du délai prévu par la Constitution, évitant ainsi de nouvelles élections anticipées.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le Parlement du Kosovo a élu l'économiste Justina Shiroka Pula à la présidence du pays, une fonction essentiellement honorifique, juste avant l'expiration du délai prévu par la Constitution, évitant ainsi de nouvelles élections anticipées. Justina Shiroka Pula a recueilli 81 voix, soit une de plus que le nombre requis, mercredi en début de matinée. Si le Parlement n'était pas parvenu à élire de nouveau président, des élections législatives anticipées auraient dû être convoquées. "Ce mandat n'appartient pas à une seule personne. Il appartient à nos citoyens. Je serai la présidente de tous les citoyens", a déclaré Justina Shiroka Pula après le vote. L'élection de Justina Shiroka Pula intervient après que le parti au pouvoir du Premier ministre Albin Kurti, Vetevendosje, et le Parti démocratique du Kosovo ont conclu un accord visant à limiter les pouvoirs du tribunal spécial de La Haye chargé de juger les crimes de guerre au Kosovo a été conclu. L'ancien président du Kosovo, Hashim Thaçi, a été [USN:L8N45802W TEXT:"condamné"] le mois dernier à 25 ans de prison pour meurtre, torture et détention illégale par ce tribunal, chargé de juger les crimes de guerre commis lors de l'insurrection de 1998-1999 qui a abouti à l'indépendance du pays. La présidence est essentiellement honorifique au Kosovo, mais elle a souvent été source d'instabilité politique, une majorité des deux tiers au Parlement étant nécessaire pour élire un président. Justina Shiroka Pula, née en 1953, est présidente de l'Académie des sciences et des arts du Kosovo et professeure d'économie. Elle a occupé le poste de ministre de l'Economie entre 2008 et 2011.

item.title: L'Iran doit réduire ses activités d'enrichissement d'uranium pour mettre fin à la guerre, dit Vance
item.description: Le vice-président américain J.D. Vance a déclaré dans une interview accordée à Reuters que l'Iran réduire de manière "significative" sa capacité d'enrichissement nucléaire pour satisfaire aux exigences des Etats-Unis et mettre fin à la guerre.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage
item.content:encoded: Le vice-président américain J.D. Vance a déclaré dans une interview accordée à Reuters que l'Iran réduire de manière "significative" sa capacité d'enrichissement nucléaire pour satisfaire aux exigences des Etats-Unis et mettre fin à la guerre. J.D. Vance avait dirigé au mois de juin une délégation américaine lors de pourparlers avec l'Iran ayant mené à la conclusion d'un accord provisoire pour mettre fin à la guerre, dénoncé depuis par les Etats-Unis. S'exprimant lundi à l'issue d'un déplacement en Alaska effectué pour soutenir le sénateur républicain Dan Sullivan en amont des élections de mi-mandat, J.D. Vance a déclaré que tout accord exigerait de l'Iran qu'il réduise sa capacité d'enrichissement nucléaire. "Si vous ne voulez pas d'arme nucléaire, alors pourquoi avez-vous besoin de combustible enrichi à 60%? Et si vous voulez montrer votre engagement à ne pas fabriquer d'arme nucléaire, ne produisez pas de combustible hautement enrichi. C'est une question fondamentale", a dit J.D. Vance. "Je pense que s'ils veulent montrer leur engagement à ne pas fabriquer d'arme nucléaire, ils devraient prendre des mesures concrètes concernant leur capacité d'enrichissement." Téhéran et les Washington ont échangé ces dernières semaines des propositions visant à mettre fin au conflit et à rouvrir le détroit d'Ormuz, une voie maritime essentielle pour le transport mondial d'énergie. Le président américain Donald Trump a rejeté la dernière offre de Téhéran et a averti que les opérations militaires pourraient s'intensifier après les élections de mi-mandat. J.D. Vance a déclaré que les Etats-Unis restaient ouverts à un accord, mais qu'ils exigeraient des concessions concrètes de la part de l'Iran en matière de nucléaire. "Nous n'allons pas troquer des paroles contre des actes", a-t-il affirmé.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS Wall Street en hausse, du répit avant la saison des résultats
item.description: La Bourse de New York a fini en hausse mardi, avec des records du S&P-500 et du Nasdaq, alors que les prix du pétrole se sont stabilisés et que les rendements obligataires ont diminué, rassurant un peu les investisseurs et leur permettant de se tourner vers la saison des résultats trimestriels qui approche.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: La Bourse de New York a fini en hausse mardi, avec des records du S&P-500 et du Nasdaq, alors que les prix du pétrole se sont stabilisés et que les rendements obligataires ont diminué, rassurant un peu les investisseurs et leur permettant de se tourner vers la saison des résultats trimestriels qui approche. L'indice Dow Jones (.DJI) a gagné 0,49%, ou 253,14 points, à 51.521,04 points. Le S&P-500 (.SPX) , plus large, a pris 45,00 points, soit 0,58%, à 7.818,95 points. Le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) a avancé de son côté de 122,48 points (0,45%) à 27.599,79 points. Un rapport du département américain du Commerce publié dans la journée montre que le déficit commercial des Etats-Unis s'est amplifié plus qu'attendu en août, pour atteindre un pic inédit, sous l'effet de la hausse des importations en raison d'une demande interne robuste qui pourrait nourrir les pressions inflationnistes. Malgré tout, selon des données FedWatch de CME, les marchés financiers misent désormais à 19,4% seulement sur une nouvelle hausse des taux de la Réserve fédérale (Fed) lors de sa réunion d'octobre après le resserrement monétaire opéré le mois dernier. La perspective de voir la banque centrale américaine relever ses taux a été alimentée par la flambée des prix du pétrole, dans le contexte de guerre entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran, avec la crainte de répercussions plus larges sur les prix. Toutefois, les craintes à l'égard de l'approvisionnement en pétrole se sont apaisées avec l'accord conclu par le G7 pour libérer des réserves - une annonce qui a contribué à stabiliser les prix du WTI et du Brent . Cela a également engendré "une baisse des rendements obligataires car (quand les prix du pétrole se stabilisent ou diminuent), il y a moins d'anxiété à propos de l'inflation, ce qui favorise ensuite la hausse du marché des actions", a commenté Oliver Pursche, vice-président de Wealthspire Advisors, à New York. "C'est ce qui a rythmé le marché ces deux dernières semaines", a-t-il ajouté. A une semaine du coup d'envoi de la saison des résultats, qui sera donné mardi prochain par plusieurs groupes financiers américains de premier plan, les analystes s'attendent à une hausse d'environ 30% des chiffres d'affaires des entreprises du S&P-500 au troisième trimestre, montrent des données LSEG. Un bond de près de 115% des résultats des firmes énergétiques est attendu, selon LSEG, ainsi qu'une hausse de plus de 66% pour les résultats des groupes technologiques. Presque tous les secteurs majeurs du S&P-500 ont fini dans le vert ce mardi. Côté valeurs, à noter, Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) a pris 5,8% après avoir revu à la hausse sa prévision de chiffre d'affaires pour l'exercice fiscal 2028, citant une forte demande pour les puces qu'il conçoit destinées aux 'data centers'. AMD (AMD.O) a terminé en hausse de 2,8% après que sa directrice générale Lisa Su a déclaré que le fabricant de semiconducteurs prévoyait d'augmenter de manière significative ses livraisons l'an prochain afin de répondre à la demande croissante pour l'intelligence artificielle (IA). Option Care Health (OPCH.O) a grimpé de 32,7% après que McKesson (MCK.N) et Clayton Dubilier & Rice sont convenus de racheter le groupe pour un montant de 5,8 milliards de dollars incluant sa dette.
