item.title: Uganda approves sale of Dangote refinery shares to domestic investors
item.description: Uganda's Capital Markets Authority has approved investors within the East African country to participate in the Dangote Petroleum Refinery's initial public offering (IPO), a statement on X showed late on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Uganda's Capital Markets Authority has approved investors within the East African country to participate in the Dangote Petroleum Refinery's initial public offering (IPO), a statement on X showed late on Tuesday. Aliko Dangote, Africa's richest man, [USN:L4N4511G5 TEXT:"launched"] a $1.6 billion initial public offering of the refinery in September, to fund a doubling of its capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day. The deal is being marketed as a "people's IPO" and would be Africa's largest. In the statement, Uganda's state-run Capital Markets Authority (CMA) said it had approved the offer of securities under the IPO of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE. The approval was granted after an application submitted on behalf of the refinery by Stanbic IBTC Capital Limited. This week [USN:L1N45R0NF TEXT:"Kenya also allowed"] its investors to participate in the IPO after its capital markets regulator approved a short-form prospectus for a global depository receipt. The Dangote refinery was built by Dangote Group over a period of 10 years at a cost of $20 billion. The refinery, which processes 700,000 barrels of crude a day on the outskirts of Lagos, has reshaped Nigeria's fuel market since it started operations in 2024.

item.title: Once shunned, Myanmar's military-backed leader set for Malaysian red carpet
item.description: Myanmar's junta chief-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing will arrive in Malaysia on Wednesday for talks with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, as the military-backed leader once shunned by regional nations seeks international legitimacy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Myanmar's junta chief-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing will arrive in Malaysia on Wednesday for talks with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, as the military-backed leader once shunned by regional nations seeks international legitimacy. The two-day visit comes as Malaysia [USN:L6N45S06O TEXT:"pushes ahead"] with a controversial move to repatriate thousands of Myanmar nationals, despite [USN:L6N45M0GV TEXT:"warnings"] from the United Nations and rights groups that returnees could face serious danger amid a raging civil war. "The visit provides the prime minister with an opportunity to sustain his direct engagement with Myanmar," the Malaysian government said in a statement on Tuesday. Key bilateral issues include the "voluntary, dignified and safe repatriation of Myanmar nationals of all ethnic groups who have been in Malaysia illegally," it added. Myanmar has been in turmoil since Min Aung Hlaing led a military coup in 2021, triggering a nationwide civil war that has killed an estimated 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million. The military engineered a widely criticised election that allowed Min Aung Hlaing, who is subject to a raft of Western sanctions, to take up a civilian role — a transition that has sparked some moves towards re-engagement with Myanmar. Although Min Aung Hlaing and other senior Myanmar officials [USN:L6N43P0W4 TEXT:"have been excluded"] from summits of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) since 2021 over their failure to implement an ASEAN-brokered peace roadmap, individual countries in the region have moved to rebuild ties with Naypyitaw. Since formally becoming president in April, Min Aung Hlaing has visited ASEAN members [USN:L6N44305P TEXT:"Thailand"], Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam, and also made trips to China, India, Russia and Belarus. DOMESTIC PRESSURE In Malaysia, following a wave of online hate speech and misinformation earlier this year, pressure on undocumented migrants and refugees has grown, particularly against Rohingya Muslims, many of whom fled a brutal 2017 military crackdown in Myanmar's Rakhine state bordering Bangladesh. Last month, Anwar [USN:L6N4580O7 TEXT:"said in a podcast"] that he would invite Min Aung Hlaing for an official visit if Myanmar accepted the return of thousands of Rohingya refugees. "Under pressure to send refugees back, Anwar needs Naypyitaw's cooperation, and a visit is the price," said Richard Horsey, senior Asia adviser at the International Crisis Group. "He says this is not recognition, but Min Aung Hlaing will present it as exactly that." Malaysia has deported around 10,000 Myanmar nationals since January, according to Anwar, who said Myanmar authorities had given assurances those returning would not be harmed. Although Malaysia has said the repatriations are strictly voluntary, the UN has raised [USN:L6N45M0GV TEXT:"concerns"] about the move, warning that people sent back to Myanmar may face serious risks. Rights groups have also [USN:L1N45F0FJ TEXT:"urged"] Malaysia to halt the returns, citing the ongoing violence and risk of forced conscription. There are about 193,000 registered refugees and asylum seekers from Myanmar in Malaysia, according to UN data. The country is not a signatory to the UN refugee convention. DEADLY AIRSTRIKES CONTINUE Despite repeated calls for an end to the violence, including from the 11-member ASEAN grouping, the civil war in Myanmar continues unabated. The Myanmar military has carried out several airstrikes within the last fortnight in Rakhine state, where it is battling a rebel group, killing at least 58 people and injuring dozens of others, including at a busy market. The attack was the deadliest since a December hospital bombing and drew [USN:L1N45L0X3 TEXT:"condemnation"] from UN Secretary-General António Guterres. In a statement to Reuters, ASEAN's current chair, the Philippines, also [USN:L6N45P01J TEXT:"expressed concern"] over the airstrike. "Nothing in the region's response gives Naypyitaw any reason to think they will come at a diplomatic cost, including Min Aung Hlaing's red carpet in Kuala Lumpur," said Crisis Group's Horsey.

item.title: Matthew Tkachuk leads Panthers to first regulation lead, win at Kings
item.description: Matthew Tkachuk gave the visiting Florida Panthers their first lead in regulation this season when he scored at 11:20 of the third period and they held on for a 2-1 win against the Los Angeles Kings on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Matthew Tkachuk gave the visiting Florida Panthers their first lead in regulation this season when he scored at 11:20 of the third period and they held on for a 2-1 win against the Los Angeles Kings on Tuesday night. Sam Bennett passed to Tkachuk trailing on a rush following a turnover in the neutral zone and he squeezed the puck between the pads of Darcy Kuemper from the left faceoff circle for a 2-1 lead. Seth Jones also scored and Jacob Markstrom made 19 saves for the Panthers in the finale of their season-opening four-game road trip. Alex Laferriere scored and Kuemper made 26 saves for the Kings, who are still winless on the season. The Kings took a 1-0 lead at 19:00 of the first period after winning a battle for the puck behind the Florida net. Los Angeles forward Erik Haula brought the puck above the goal line and took a shot from the bottom of the right circle that was blocked by Niko Mikkola, but the puck came to Laferriere at the bottom of the opposite circle and he swept it into the net. After the Kings could not take advantage of a 5-on-3 power play that lasted 1:21 and bridged the first and second periods, the Panthers tied it seconds later. Lars Eller fed Jones coming down the left side just as Dmitry Kulikov was coming out of the penalty box. Jones skated around Kings forward Artemi Panarin before scoring from in close to tie it 1-1 at 3:49 of the second. Panthers forward Eetu Luostarinen limped to the locker room midway through the second period after getting hit by a shot but quickly returned. Florida forward Brad Marchand, however, did not return after his leg folded awkwardly beneath him while driving to the net in the final minute of the second period. A four-minute high-sticking double minor was called on Brandt Clarke, but the Panthers could not take the lead during that span. The Panthers lost team captain Aleksander Barkov to a lower-body injury against the San Jose Sharks last Thursday, and he was subsequently placed on long-term injured reserve. --Field Level Media

item.title: Des marins disparus en mer Noire après une frappe de drone sur leur navire au large de la Bulgarie
item.description: L'équipage d'un navire marchand est porté disparu après que leur bateau a coulé à la suite d'une attaque de drone subie pendant qu'il naviguait dans la zone économique bulgare de la mer Noire, a déclaré le Premier ministre bulgare, Rouman Radev, qualifiant l'incident de violation flagrante du droit international.
item.dc:creator: Alex Lefkowitz
item.content:encoded: L'équipage d'un navire marchand est porté disparu après que leur bateau a coulé à la suite d'une attaque de drone subie pendant qu'il naviguait dans la zone économique bulgare de la mer Noire, a déclaré le Premier ministre bulgare, Rouman Radev, qualifiant l'incident de violation flagrante du droit international. On ignore à ce stade qui est à l'origine de cette attaque menée par des drones aériens et maritimes à environ 112 kilomètres au large de la ville côtière de Byala, dans l'est de la Bulgarie, pays membre de l'Union européenne et de l'Otan. Selon des sources du secteur maritime, il s'agirait de la première attaque de ce type dans les eaux bulgares. Le ministre ukrainien des Affaires étrangères, Andriy Sybiha, a accusé la Russie d'être à l'origine de cette attaque. La Russie n'a fait aucun commentaire au sujet de l'incident. La Bulgarie n'a de frontière avec aucun de ces deux pays, mais elle occupe une position stratégique en mer Noire, où l'Ukraine et la Russie disposent toutes deux de ports importants. Une source proche de la sécurité maritime a dit que les premières analyses de l'attaque laissaient penser qu’il s’agissait probablement d’une attaque russe. Rouman Radev n’a pas précisé qui était à l'origine de l’attaque mais a fait référence à la guerre menée par la Russie en Ukraine. "Si cette guerre n'est pas arrêtée à temps, elle continuera à s'étendre géographiquement et à accroître le risque d’un conflit mondial", a-t-il déclaré. "Nous assistons à une intensification de la guerre, avec la violation de toutes les règles du droit international et des attaques contre des navires civils en mer. C’est absolument inacceptable", a-t-il ajouté. DEUXIÈME INCIDENT EN DEUX JOURS EN MER NOIRE Deux navires ont été touchés lors de l’attaque, a précisé le Premier ministre bulgare lors d'une allocution télévisée. L’équipage de l'un d’entre eux, qui transportait des céréales, a été secouru - deux personnes ont été blessées. L'autre navire, qui a coulé, battait pavillon togolais et sa cargaison n’a pas été divulguée. Une opération de recherche a été lancée pour retrouver les membres d’équipage portés disparus et détecter tout signe de menace environnementale. La présidente de la Commission européenne, Ursula von der Leyen, a déclaré de son côté que les attaques contre les bateaux civils étaient inacceptables. "Des navires commerciaux - et leurs équipages innocents - sont pris pour cible et des vies ont déjà été perdues en mer", a-t-elle déclaré. Le groupe britannique de gestion des risques maritimes Vanguard a noté que les attaques de ce mardi avaient visé le navire de fret général ALFA WATAN, battant pavillon du Togo, et le navire de fret général ABLE, battant pavillon des Palaos, précisant qu'ils se trouvaient dans la zone économique de la Bulgarie. Les deux navires ont émis des signaux de détresse et des sources bulgares ont affirmé qu’ils avaient été touchés par des drones, précise Vanguard dans un rapport. Dans un message publié sur la plate-forme X, Andrij Sybiha estime que la Russie a créé "une dangereuse chaîne de conséquences" en s'en prenant à la marine marchande civile. "En attaquant des navires civils, elle rend la navigation difficile. En rendant la navigation difficile, elle fait grimper les risques, les primes d'assurance et les coûts de transport, et menace l'approvisionnement des marchés mondiaux en denrées alimentaires", ajoute-t-il. Cette nouvelle attaque de drone en mer Noire fait suite à un incident rapporté lundi par les autorités roumaines : elles ont alors déclaré que deux personnes avaient trouvé la mort dans l'incendie d'un navire en mer Noire, en dehors des eaux territoriales de la Roumanie. Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky a accusé une attaque de drone russe d'avoir été à l'origine de cet incendie, qui a entraîné le naufrage de ce navire. Depuis l'invasion de l’Ukraine par la Russie en 2022, les pays européens ont signalé à plusieurs reprises des intrusions de drones russes dans leur espace aérien, ainsi que la présence de mines flottantes sur des routes commerciales en mer Noire.

item.title: Brussels looks to capture Big Tech through tax on large corporations, FT reports
item.description: Brussels is considering taxing big US tech companies through a broad levy on large corporations in an effort to raise revenues for the EU while avoiding a backlash from the Trump administration, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brussels is considering taxing big US tech companies through a broad levy on large corporations in an effort to raise revenues for the EU while avoiding a backlash from the Trump administration, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday. The European Commission was working on new ways to capture more income from tech groups such as Apple (AAPL.O) , Meta (META.O) and Google (GOOGL.O) without singling them out, the newspaper reported, citing six officials with knowledge of the discussions. Brussels was considering changes to its "Corporate Resource for Europe" (CORE) proposal that would require all companies operating in the EU with revenue of more than €100 million ($112.32 million) a year to pay an annual lump-sum tax contribution, the report said. In its current form, [USN:L8N41710O TEXT:"CORE"] requires these companies to pay a fixed annual levy of between €100,000 and €750,000, capturing only a small portion of a multinational company’s earnings. "Some EU capitals are opposed to a pure digital tax because they don’t want to upset the Americans, and many more are opposed to CORE," an EU official told the FT. "The solution is to expand (the tax) to cover pretty much all the big companies." Reuters could not immediately verify the report. The European Commission, the Computer & Communications Industry Association (CCIA), which represents several US tech companies, Apple, Google and Meta did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment outside regular business hours. US President Donald Trump in [USN:L1N42Y0MO TEXT:"June"] threatened a 100% tariff on all goods from any country that imposes a digital services tax on American companies. The US Trade Representative's office, which has long threatened European countries with retaliatory tariffs if they impose such taxes, has argued that these levies discriminate against US companies, which dominate the sector globally. ($1 = 0.8903 euros)

item.title: Russia says it launched 'massive' strikes on Kyiv, other areas of Ukraine
item.description: Russia's defence ministry said on Wednesday its forces had carried out a "massive strike" on military-industrial facilities in Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions, using high-precision land-, sea- and air-launched weapons, as well as drones.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia's defence ministry said on Wednesday its forces had carried out a "massive strike" on military-industrial facilities in Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions, using high-precision land-, sea- and air-launched weapons, as well as drones. Targets included sites where the company Fire Point makes and stores Flamingo cruise missiles and medium- and long-range drones in Kyiv as well as regions of Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kirovohrad, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava and Kharkiv, it said. The strikes targeted port and ship-repair infrastructure in the Odesa region, as well as vessels it said were being used in the interests of Ukraine's armed forces, the ministry added.

item.title: Intel to keep working on Musk's Terafab chipmaking venture, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: Intel Corp will continue to work with Elon Musk on his Terafab project, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Intel Corp (INTC.O) will continue to work with Elon Musk on his Terafab project, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday. Here's what to know: Intel will remain involved in the project, CEO Lip-Bu Tan told Bloomberg ahead of an event in Tokyo marking the US chipmaker's 50th year of operations in Japan. Intel and Tesla did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside regular business hours. Last week, Tesla (TSLA.O) and SpaceX (SPCX.O) CEO Elon Musk said on X that there were discussions over potential cooperation between Taiwan chip major TSMC (2330.TW) and his chipmaking project, Terafab. Responding on X to a screenshot of an article headlined "TSMC Exploring Plans to Work With Elon Musk's TeraFab," Musk wrote on Saturday: "Just discussions, but something may come of it". A potential involvement by TSMC could likely challenge Intel's role in Terafab, as Musk [USN:L4N40Q0ZY TEXT:"weighs partners"] for the chipmaking venture.

item.title: Bond selloff leaves France no room for fiscal mistakes, Citadel executive says
item.description: France no longer has any room for mistakes to get its fiscal house in order, and pressure from financial markets should help focus minds in Paris on reining in spending ahead of next year's presidential election, senior Citadel executive Angel Ubide told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Leigh Thomas, Gabriel Stargardter
item.content:encoded: France no longer has any room for mistakes to get its fiscal house in order, and pressure from financial markets should help focus minds in Paris on reining in spending ahead of next year's presidential election, senior Citadel executive Angel Ubide told Reuters. France has seen its borrowing costs surge in the current global bond rout, prompting a selloff in the euro, as investors worry its fragile public finances risk spilling over to the rest of Europe. Ubide, head of Economic Research for Fixed Income & Macro at Citadel, which has $76 billion in assets under management, said France doesn't pose a systemic risk to Europe - yet. "France is very big. If we are discussing a systemic problem with France, we are discussing a systemic problem for Europe. I would hope and expect that we don't get to the point of having that discussion," Ubide told Reuters in an interview. As well as the presidential vote, it is also key that parliamentary elections produce a majority capable of reining in public finances, Ubide said. "So I think the market pressure in that sense is helpful because it's sending a clear signal that you have no room for mistakes - that is the most important thing," he said. France's bond market turbulence has [USN:L6N45S0D2 TEXT:"raised concerns"] in financial markets that it could trigger a broader fallout hitting other euro zone countries and the euro. [USN:L8N45H174 TEXT:"ECB policymakers"] and France's [USN:S8N3XB0C2 TEXT:"finance minister"] have so far ruled out any need for the European Central Bank [USN:L1N45N0CH TEXT:"to step in"] and stabilise the market. The yield on France's 10-year bonds [USN:L8N45O0YO TEXT:"briefly hit"] a 24-year high of over 5% last week. Meanwhile, the euro hit 17-month lows below $1.12 on Monday and tumbled against sterling , the Swiss franc and Japan's yen . ELECTION AND PROTESTS RAMP UP INSTABILITY France's presidential election is approaching against a backdrop of [USN:L1N45S0C7 TEXT:"student protests"], rising prices and pinched wallets, prompting disgruntled voters to desert mainstream parties in favour of far-right and far-left parties, which are surging ahead in polls. Marine Le Pen, the far-right frontrunner in the polls, sought on Tuesday to establish her [USN:L1N45S0C4 TEXT:"budget"] credibility, pledging a steep increase in her plans to cut spending if elected. She said she would target budget savings of €140 billion ($157.6 billion) over the course of a five-year presidency and enshrine deficit reduction in the constitution through a referendum. However, her proposals have met with scepticism from economists who spoke to Reuters. They questioned whether cuts of that scale could be achieved, especially as she gave few details on whether she plans to stick with a policy for reducing the retirement age for some workers. "There is still a big unknown, 'Who is the true Marine Le Pen?' We are still learning, and it will take time for the market to develop a view," Ubide said. ($1 = 0.8883 euros)

item.title: Selección de fútbol México finaliza gira en EEUU con derrota ante Chile
item.description: La selección mexicana de fútbol sufrió el martes una derrota por 2-0 ante su similar de Chile en el cierre de la gira por Estados Unidos que marcó el inicio de la gestión de Rafael Márquez como director técnico.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La selección mexicana de fútbol sufrió el martes una derrota por 2-0 ante su similar de Chile en el cierre de la gira por Estados Unidos que marcó el inicio de la gestión de Rafael Márquez como director técnico. Además de la derrota ante Chile, México empató por 1-1 ante Colombia y Perú, y fue goleado 3-0 por Estados Unidos, en la gira posterior a la presentación de Márquez como su director técnico el 10 de septiembre. "El principal objetivo era ver a todos los jugadores y hemos visto quién puede estar y quién no, tenemos que seguir trabajando porque hay mucho margen de mejora. Dentro del proyecto pudimos dar oportunidad a gente joven que queríamos ver, ya sacaremos después conclusiones, ahora hay que pasar la página y prepararnos para lo que viene", dijo Márquez en conferencia de prensa tras el partido. En el último partido de la gira, disputado en el Memorial Coliseum de Los Ángeles, México estuvo cerca de anotar en el minuto cinco con un peligroso disparo de Jesús Gallardo que desvió el portero chileno Lawrence Vigouroux. Chile respondió a los 11 minutos con un disparo de Gonzalo Tapia que atajó el portero Alex Padilla. La selección sudamericana volvió a poner en peligro la portería de México a los 28 minutos con un disparo de Maximiliano Gutiérrez que salió muy cerca del poste izquierdo. Vigouroux evitó de nueva cuenta el gol de México al lanzarse para desviar un potente disparo de Roberto Alvarado a los 32 minutos. El portero chileno volvió a salvar su portería a los 48 minutos al desviar un disparo de Obed Vargas. Chile se puso en ventaja a los 54 minutos cuando Gutiérrez escapó por velocidad tras un pase de Tapia y definió de derecha ante la salida del portero. El segundo gol de Chile cayó a los 65 minutos cuando Vicente Pizarro aprovechó un error defensivo de Johan Vásquez, quien no pudo cortar un pase de Darío Osorio, para definir de zurda ante la salida de Padilla. "Lo importante es que vimos a varios jugadores jóvenes y a gente que necesitamos saber cómo se comportaba, para esto eran los partidos amistosos. Ya sabemos, para el próximo compromiso, a la gente que tenemos que llevar a ese tipo de partidos", apuntó Márquez. México tendrá que mostrar un mejor funcionamiento para sus próximos compromisos que serán en noviembre cuando enfrente a Jamaica a visita recíproca en los cuartos de final de la Liga de Naciones de la Concacaf.

item.title: Golden Knights score 3 special teams goals, rout Kraken
item.description: Tomas Hertl scored two goals and had two assists and Jack Eichel added a goal and three assists as the visiting Vegas Golden Knights cruised to a 6-2 victory over the Seattle Kraken on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tomas Hertl scored two goals and had two assists and Jack Eichel added a goal and three assists as the visiting Vegas Golden Knights cruised to a 6-2 victory over the Seattle Kraken on Tuesday night. Victor Olofsson also scored two goals before leaving in the third period with an apparent left leg injury, while Mark Stone recorded a short-handed goal and an assist for Vegas. Carter Hart made 25 saves for the Golden Knights, who completed a sweep of a two-game Pacific Northwest road trip that began with a 3-2 victory at Vancouver on Sunday. Shane Wright and Jared McCann scored goals and Kaapo Kakko had two assists for Seattle. Joey Daccord, who entered the game having stopped 56 of 58 shots in two wins, allowed five goals on 21 shots before being pulled after two periods. Philipp Grubauer finished up and made six saves, allowing one Vegas score. Olofsson gave Vegas a 1-0 lead at the 13:02 mark of the first period when Rasmus Andersson's blast from the right point deflected in off his left skate. The Golden Knights extended the lead near the end of the period on a power-play goal by Hertl, who slammed in a pass by Stone. Stone finished a 2-on-1 short-handed break with Eichel with a snap shot from the left circle to make 3-0 early in the second period. It was Stone's 400th point in 404 games with the Golden Knights, 17 points off the team record of 417 held by Jonathan Marchessault. Olofsson scored his team-leading fourth goal midway through the period when he snapped a shot from the bottom of the right circle in off the far left post. Eichel made it 5-0 with 31 seconds left in the period when he stole the puck from Bobby McMann along the boards and then went in on a breakaway and snapped a shot past Daccord's glove side. Seattle broke up the shutout at the 4:52 mark of the third period when Wright fired a wrist shot from the high slot past Hart's glove side. Hertl extended the lead to 6-1 with a power-play goal after Kraken center Ben Meyers picked up a five-minute match major and game misconduct for a boarding penalty on Olofsson, who had to be helped off the ice. McCann finished the scoring with a power-play goal with five minutes to go, roofing a wrist shot from the left circle past Hart's blocker side. --Field Level Media

item.title: Hedge funds warn BoE repo reforms could backfire
item.description: A hedge fund industry group has warned the Bank of England that proposed reforms to the market for short-term loans secured against UK government bonds, known as "repo", could backfire and reduce liquidity at times of market stress.
item.dc:creator: Phoebe Seers, Iain Withers
item.content:encoded: A hedge fund industry group has warned the Bank of England that proposed reforms to the market for short-term loans secured against UK government bonds, known as "repo", could backfire and reduce liquidity at times of market stress. Industry body Alternative Investment Management Association wrote to the BoE this month in a letter, seen by Reuters, that implementing proposed central clearing in the market could create "new vulnerabilities" and expose investors to more volatility. It marks a more direct warning after the lobby's response last year to the central bank's initial proposals, which flagged "significant structural issues." A global bond market selloff has put soaring borrowing costs in the spotlight, including in Britain, where 30-year yields on government bonds, or gilts, jumped to [USN:L8N45N0EJ TEXT:"their highest since 1998"] earlier this month. Supervisors and financial authorities are watching closely the growing role of hedge funds in sovereign bond markets. The [USN:L6N45R0Z5 TEXT:"IMF said"] on Tuesday that hedge funds had grown their presence in the market, while the BoE has previously said that greater activity of leveraged hedge funds in the gilt market has introduced new risks. The BoE is conducting a consultation on proposals aimed at making the gilt repo market more resilient, including by expanding central clearing, in which a central body stands between buyers and sellers and guarantees trades. It also calls for minimum haircuts, or discounts on non-centrally cleared repo transactions, as a way of better protecting lenders and reducing the risk of asset fire sales during periods of market stress. The proposed changes were in response to the 2020 "Dash for Cash" and the 2022 liability-driven investment crisis that exposed vulnerabilities that amplified market stress and ultimately required central bank intervention. In a sign of growing concern, AIMA told the BoE this month that members had raised new questions about any further expansion of central clearing. In a letter signed by its global head of markets Adam Jacobs-Dean, AIMA said the changes could encourage hedge funds to rely on shorter-term daily repo financing rather than typical two-week deals, which in turn could leave investors more exposed to disruption in funding markets. AIMA did not directly reference the recent global selloff in bond markets but said the planned reforms could lead to “greater volatility during times of market stress”. The letter was in response to an article on the BoE’s website by Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden that said similar initiatives were being pursued internationally, notably in the US Treasury market which will mandate central clearing for all Treasury repo borrowing from next year. AIMA said that the BoE should wait to see how the US clearing mandate works before implementing it. The BoE, which has said any reforms would likely take years, not months, declined to comment. The central bank has yet to decide on which proposals to take forward. Breeden said in July that "doing nothing is not an option", warning that banks could pull repo financing more aggressively in a severe market shock. Net borrowing in the gilt repo market — where traders seek to profit from moves in interest rates, and investors turn bond holdings into temporary cash — totals around £200 billion ($270 billion) according to BoE data, £85 billion of which is by hedge funds.

item.title: Israelis mark three years since Hamas attack that set off Gaza assault
item.description: Israelis will hold a vigil at the site of the Nova music festival near the Gaza border, where 348 young people were killed by militants during the attack on October 7, 2023.
item.dc:creator: Steven Scheer
item.content:encoded: Israelis will on Wednesday mark three years since Hamas attacked Israel on October 7, 2023, triggering a military assault that destroyed much of Gaza , where conditions remain dire despite a [USN:L6N45Q023 TEXT:"year-old ceasefire"] that is meant to halt the war for good. The attacks, during which militants killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostages to Gaza, marked the deadliest day in Israel's history. Israel's subsequent bombardment and ground operations have killed more than 74,000 people in Gaza, health authorities there say. On Wednesday, Israelis will hold a vigil at the site of the Nova music festival near the Gaza border, where 348 young people were killed by militants during the attack. They will also hold an event commemorating the anniversary at Hostage Square in Tel Aviv. ISRAELI ELECTION 20 DAYS AWAY The anniversary is the first for Israelis without any hostages still held in Gaza, with those dead and alive exchanged in swaps with Hamas for Palestinians held in Israeli jails. The remains of the last Israeli hostage were recovered in January. It also comes just 20 days ahead of Israel's first election since the attack, a vote that is viewed as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's long tenure in power. Netanyahu has rejected blame for the security breach and resisted calls for an independent investigation. That has frustrated many in Israel, including families of those killed in the attacks, some of whom have [USN:L8N45F0EA TEXT:"joined the election race"]. A poll by the Israel Democracy Institute showed that 68% of Jewish Israelis said that the events of October 7 were a very central or fairly central element in their decision of which party to vote for. Election polls show neither Netanyahu nor his main competitors would muster enough seats in parliament to form a coalition if a vote were held today. US-BACKED CEASEFIRE FAILS TO HALT ISRAELI ATTACKS, DISARM HAMAS The anniversary is also the first since an October 10, 2025, US-brokered ceasefire deal that halted major fighting but has failed to stop Israeli attacks in Gaza or secure the disarmament of Hamas and other militant groups. The deal left Israel in control of some 53% of Gaza, since expanded by Israeli forces to nearly two-thirds. Hamas controls the remaining third, where the [USN:L8N45L0U7 TEXT:"2 million population"] mostly [USN:L1N45O05B TEXT:"live in makeshift tents"] and bombed out buildings. US President Donald Trump's so-called "Board of Peace" has proposed several plans that would see Gaza rebuilt. But those plans, which fail to account for the property rights of Palestinians whose homes were destroyed, have failed to gain the buy-in of Israel or Hamas, which are still deadlocked in ceasefire talks. The two have yet to agree on the terms of a deal that would see Hamas lay down its weapons in exchange for Israeli troop withdrawals. Israel says it will not pull back until Hamas fully disarms; Hamas says it has agreed to a phased process but will not disarm so long as Israeli attacks continue. Israel has kept up a bombing campaign in Gaza that has killed a number of Hamas militants in recent months but has also killed many civilians, say Gaza health authorities, whose death figures do not distinguish between civilians and combatants. More than 1,400 Palestinians in Gaza have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire, the health authorities say. During the same time, five Israeli soldiers have been killed by militants or in combat, the military says.

item.content:encoded: Der Medienkonzern Skydance hat am Dienstag die 110 Milliarden Dollar schwere Übernahme von Warner Bros. Discovery abgeschlossen. Damit entsteht unter der Führung von Vorstandschef David Ellison ein neuer Hollywood-Gigant. Der Deal vereint die Filmstudios hinter Erfolgen wie "Mission: Impossible" und "Harry Potter" mit Fernseh- und Streaming-Sendern wie CBS, CNN, Paramount+ und HBO Max. Ziel sei es, es "mit den größten Akteuren unserer Branche aufzunehmen", sagte Ellison in einer Mitteilung an die Mitarbeiter. Die Fusion findet in einer Zeit statt, in der die traditionelle Medienbranche durch sinkende Kabel-TV-Abonnements und den teuren Wettbewerb im Streaming-Geschäft unter Druck steht. Die etablierte Branche sei selbstgefällig gewesen und habe zugelassen, dass Konkurrenten wie Netflix und Amazon ihr Geschäft umkrempelten, sagte Ellison auf einer Pressekonferenz. Auf dem neuen Konzern, der ebenfalls Skydance heißen wird, lasten Schulden von rund 80 Milliarden Dollar. Geplant ist unter anderem, die Streaming-Dienste wie HBO Max und Paramount+ zusammenzulegen und Einsparungen von sechs Milliarden Dollar zu realisieren. US-Präsident Donald Trump äußerte sich zustimmend zu dem Geschäft. Die Fusion hatte im Vorfeld jedoch Bedenken wegen der redaktionellen Unabhängigkeit der zum Konzern gehörenden Nachrichtensender ausgelöst. Als Teil der Einigung zur Genehmigung des Deals stimmte Ellison der Schaffung eines redaktionellen Aufsichtsgremiums für CNN und CBS zu. Kritiker befürchten jedoch, dass dieses Gremium "zahnlos" sein wird. Die Sorgen werden durch frühere Vorwürfe geschürt, Ellison habe die Berichterstattung bei CBS News zugunsten von Trump beeinflusst.

item.description: Dos sindicatos de la mina de cobre chilena Centinela dijeron el miércoles que las negociaciones contractuales con Antofagasta Minerals fracasaron por lo que iniciarán la huelga en el primer turno de la jornada.
item.dc:creator: Fabián Andrés Cambero
item.content:encoded: Dos sindicatos de la mina de cobre chilena Centinela dijeron el miércoles que las negociaciones contractuales con Antofagasta Minerals fracasaron por lo que iniciarán la huelga en el primer turno de la jornada. El riesgo de una paralización había estado apoyando los precios globales del cobre en momentos en que la producción del metal se ha visto restringida por diversos problemas operativos, eventos naturales y bajas leyes de mineral. "Este fracaso en las conversaciones se produjo tras la negativa a abordar un mecanismo que ponga término a la discriminación y que prevenga que ella no se produzca durante la vigencia del contrato colectivo", dijeron los sindicatos en un comunicado. La paralización inicia a las 8.00 hora local (1100 GMT). "La huelga legal tiene una justeza y legitimidad innegable, la que se mantendrá de forma ordenada y pacífica, por todo el tiempo necesario hasta alcanzar una resolución favorable", agregaron. Los sindicatos Minera Esperanza y Distrito Centinela, que suman 708 socios, buscan que todos los trabajadores reciban el mismo nivel de beneficios independiente del sindicato al que se encuentren afiliados.

item.content:encoded: Die französische Regierung ist einem Zeitungsbericht zufolge notfalls bereit, das Parlament bei der Verabschiedung des Haushalts für 2027 zu umgehen. Um milliardenschwere Ausgabenkürzungen durchzusetzen, könnten spezielle verfassungsmäßige Befugnisse eingesetzt werden, falls die Verhandlungen ins Stocken geraten, berichtete die Zeitung "Wall Street Journal" am Dienstag unter Berufung auf Finanzminister Roland Lescure. Dieser hat dem Blatt zufolge zwar Verhandlungsbereitschaft signalisiert, will jedoch bei zwei Punkten nicht nachgeben: Das Haushaltsdefizit dürfe maximal fünf Prozent des Bruttoinlandsprodukts betragen, und es dürfe keine Änderungen geben, die das Wirtschaftswachstum beeinträchtigten. Die französische Regierung will mit einem harten Sparkurs das hohe Haushaltsdefizit senken und das Vertrauen der Finanzmärkte zurückgewinnen. Sie legte einen Haushaltsentwurf für 2027 vor, der Einsparungen von insgesamt 54 Milliarden Euro vorsieht. Darunter sind auch unpopuläre Maßnahmen, um die Nervosität der Anleiheinvestoren vor der Präsidentschaftswahl im kommenden Jahr zu besänftigen. In der Bevölkerung wächst der Unmut über die Sparpläne. Beschäftigte des öffentlichen Dienstes streikten bereits gegen den geplanten Lohnstopp. Die Proteste von Schülern gegen mangelnde Mittel für Schulen weiten sich aus. Am Dienstag kam es erneut zu Zusammenstößen zwischen Demonstranten und der Polizei. Ministerpräsident Sebastien Lecornu bezeichnete den Sparkurs aber als notwendig, um das Haushaltsdefizit in den Griff zu bekommen. Seine beiden Vorgänger waren über ihre Sparpläne gestürzt, und seit den vorgezogenen Parlamentswahlen 2024 verfügt die Regierung über keine eigene Mehrheit mehr.

item.dc:creator: Andreas Rinke, Holger Hansen
item.content:encoded: Die Bundesanwaltschaft hat den früheren Präsidenten des Bundesnachrichtendienstes (BND), August Hanning, wegen des Verdachts der Spionage und des Landesverrats festnehmen lassen. Auch ein ehemaliger hochrangiger BND-Mitarbeiter sei verhaftet worden, teilte die Karlsruher Behörde am Dienstag mit. Hanning wird unter anderem landesverräterische Ausspähung, versuchter Landesverrat und geheimdienstliche Agententätigkeit vorgeworfen. Der Ex-BND-Mitarbeiter Manfred D. soll als mutmaßlicher Komplize Beihilfe geleistet haben. Offen blieb zunächst, an welches Land Hanning vertrauliche Informationen weitergegeben haben soll. Dem "Spiegel" zufolge könnte es sich um Aserbaidschan handeln. Die Ermittler gingen dem Verdacht nach, dass der Ex-BND-Chef eine Analyse für den Geheimdienst der Kaukasusrepublik erstellt haben könnte. Die Bundesanwaltschaft wollte den Bericht nicht kommentieren. Hanning war von 1998 bis 2005 BND-Präsident. Von 2005 bis 2009 arbeitete er als Staatssekretär im Bundesinnenministerium. Laut Bundesanwaltschaft soll er über Jahre hinweg geheime BND-Dokumente von Manfred D. erhalten und für eine private Beratertätigkeit genutzt haben. Manfred D. war Hannings Büroleiter und hatte diese Funktion auch unter dessen Nachfolgern bis März 2026 inne. Demnach soll er Hanning bis Juni 2022 gegen Geld fast 2000 Dokumente zur Verfügung gestellt haben, darunter vielfach als Verschlusssache eingestufte Informationen für die Leitungsebene. In einem Fall soll Hanning die geheimen Informationen genutzt haben, um eine Analyse für den Mitarbeiter eines ausländischen Geheimdienstes zu erstellen. Zudem habe er über Jahre hinweg einen Angehörigen eines anderen staatlichen Nachrichtendienstes mit politischen Informationen versorgt. Die Ermittlungen kamen den Angaben zufolge ins Rollen, nachdem bei Hanning im September 2025 in einem anderen Verfahren der Staatsanwaltschaft Hamburg Beweismittel gefunden worden waren. Die beiden Beschuldigten sollen nun einem Ermittlungsrichter des Bundesgerichtshofs vorgeführt werden. Im Rahmen des Verfahrens gab es am Dienstag Durchsuchungen an mehreren Orten in Deutschland. Die beiden Festnahmen durch das Bundeskriminalamt erfolgten in Bayern und Nordrhein-Westfalen. "Der BND hat frühzeitig und unverzüglich umfangreiche interne Ermittlungen einleiten lassen, die den Verdacht erhärteten", teilte der aktuelle BND-Präsident Martin Jäger mit. "Für den BND und mich gibt es bei der internen Sicherheit keine Kompromisse. Keines meiner Ziele, keine meiner Prioritäten wird durch diesen Vorgang in Frage gestellt." Erst am Montag hatte Jäger vor einer verschärften Sicherheitslage und einem möglichen gewalttätigen Konflikt mit Russland gewarnt. Er sprach von einem "Schattenkrieg", den Russland gegen den Westen und vor allem Deutschland führe. Offenbar stand Russland aber nicht auf der Liste der Länder, die Hanning mit Informationen versorgt haben soll. Als möglich gilt, dass der ehemalige BND-Chef etwa Staaten wie Israel vertrauliche Papiere zugespielt haben könnte. Die deutschen Geheimdienste hatten seit längerem angekündigt, dass sie wegen der verschärften geopolitischen Lage sofort auf alle Verdachtsfälle auch in ihren Häusern reagieren würden. PARTEIEN REAGIEREN MIT KRITIK, LOB UND FORDERUNGEN Die Fraktionschefs der SPD- und CDU/CSU-Bundestagsfraktion, Matthias Miersch und Thorsten Frei, äußerten sich entsetzt und forderten Aufklärung. Frei sprach von einer "verstörenden Nachricht". Mit Blick auf die Beratung im Parlament über die Geheimdienste-Reform fügte er hinzu, man werde von überall her angegriffen. Die Reform sei dringend nötig. Miersch sprach von einem "alarmierenden Vorgang". Er forderte eine Debatte über Karenzzeiten von ausscheidenden Geheimdienst-Mitarbeitern. Auch der SPD-Bundestagsabgeordnete und Geheimdienstkontrolleur Daniel Baldy forderte schärfere Regeln für ehemalige Spitzenkräfte der Nachrichtendienste. Wer als BND-Präsident oder in einer anderen sicherheitsempfindlichen Funktion tätig gewesen sei, dürfe anschließend nicht in einer privaten Beratungsfirma arbeiten. Die stellvertretende Linken-Fraktionschefin Clara Bünger sagte, die Ermittlungen gegen Hanning zeigten erneut, dass die Geheimdienste selbst ein Sicherheitsrisiko seien. Das wisse man nicht erst seit den Verstrickungen des Verfassungsschutzes in die Mordserie der Neonazi-Terroristen vom NSU.

item.title: England have put World Cup disappointment behind them, says Tuchel
item.description: England have moved on from their World Cup semi-final disappointment and taken an important step forward with their performances in the Nations League, manager Thomas Tuchel said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: England have moved on from their World Cup semi-final disappointment and taken an important step forward with their performances in the Nations League, manager Thomas Tuchel said. After suffering a [USN:L1N45I06S TEXT:"3-2 defeat "]by world champions Spain in their Nations League opener, England responded with home and away wins over the Czech Republic and a 7-0 thrashing of Croatia, scoring 14 goals in their opening four matches. Tuchel, who has continued to face questions about England's 2-1 World Cup [USN:L8N43H27Q TEXT:"semi-final loss"] to Argentina, said the team had built on the progress made in the tournament in North America rather than starting from scratch as they target success at Euro 2028 on home soil. "I think it's necessary to move on," the 53-year-old told reporters after Tuesday's [USN:L8N45S1VY TEXT:"3-0 win over the Czechs"] at Wembley. "I can only repeat that we didn't go out in the group stage, sometimes it feels like that, but we didn't. "There was criticism and scepticism around, but I said we don't have to start completely new because we can build on what we achieved together. We played some high-level competitive football in the World Cup. "Now we move to the next step and it's always important to take the next step. The commitment and attitude of the players from the first day in camp have been at a very high level and I'm happy that we have shown it in all four matches." England resume their Nations League campaign against Croatia on November 12.

item.content:encoded: The Indian central bank [USN:L1N45T036 TEXT:"raised its benchmark repo rate"] INREPO=ECI by 25 basis points to 5.5% on Wednesday, marking the first rise in nearly four years amid mounting inflation and strong economic growth. COMMENTARY: AASTHA GUDWANI, INDIA CHIEF ECONOMIST, BARCLAYS, MUMBAI "We found today's policy statement and tonality quite neutral. By changing the stance to 'calibrated tightening', we think the RBI has tempered the expectation of back-to-back hikes. We expect one more 25bp hike in remainder of FY27 but it may not necessarily come in December (more likely in February 2027)." ADITI NAYAR, CHIEF ECONOMIST, ICRA, DELHI "Today's policy outcome is in line with our expectations of a rate hike with a change in stance to clearly signal that rate cuts are off the table. The inflation prints are expected to harden moving forward, on account of a combination of factors such as the poor monsoon, rising commodity prices and an unfavourable base effect, setting the stage for another rate hike in December 2026. as of now, we do not foresee the need for further rate tightening in 2027." DHIRAJ NIM, ECONOMIST AND FX STRATEGIST, ANZ RESEARCH, MUMBAI "This is a clean and effective policy indicating that repo rate will likely go higher. But how high, will depend upon the second-order inflation impact. We expect two more hikes at the least." SAKSHI GUPTA, PRINCIPAL ECONOMIST, HDFC BANK, GURUGRAM "The RBI began its rate-hiking cycle in lockstep with the turn in the interest rates higher by global central banks. The decision to change the stance to calibrated tightening signals that today's rate hike is the beginning of a rate-hiking cycle over the coming months. We expect another 50 to 75 bps rate hikes over the coming months." "In the event that the West Asia conflict lingers on and oil prices remain elevated, the inflation risk could increase further, necessitating a more aggressive tightening cycle." KRISHNA BHIMAVARAPU, APAC ECONOMIST, STATE STREET INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT, BENGALURU "The RBI has taken a sensible first step with a 25-bps hike. Our base case remains for a 100 bps of cumulative tightening over this cycle, although the ultimate magnitude will depend on how the global energy shock, food inflation, broader inflation dynamics and the global tightening cycle evolve in the coming quarters." "If food, energy and electricity inflation begin reinforcing each other, the RBI may ultimately need to deliver significantly more tightening than today's move alone." MADHAVI ARORA, CHIEF ECONOMIST, EMKAY GLOBAL, MUMBAI "The change in stance to another new nomenclature 'calibrated tightening' felt more like a forward guidance than a policy stance per se, but has prepared markets for a higher-for-longer interest rate environment." "With US rates and growth higher and inflation proving stickier, India may need to offer a meaningly higher risk premium, particularly amid elevated global volatility, high oil prices and lacklustre natural dollar inflows. Global financial conditions could thus increasingly dictate the RBI's reaction function, alongside growth and inflation dynamics." "We maintain a (forecast for) cumulative rate hike(s) of 75 bps in this cycle, but will be watchful of the fluid global dynamics." GAURA SENGUPTA, CHIEF ECONOMIST, IDFC FIRST BANK, MUMBAI "The key surprise was the stance change to calibrated tightening and the lack of usage of normalisation of policy rate. This indicates that, in RBI's assessment, the rate-hiking cycle could be deeper." DIPTI DESHPANDE, SENIOR DIRECTOR AND PRINCIPAL ECONOMIST, CRISIL, MUMBAI "Retail inflation has firmed in recent months, while upside risks from crude oil, commodities and food prices have become more pronounced. A 'calibrated tightening' stance allows the central bank the choice to either hike rates or take a pause depending on evolving inflation conditions." "We see room for another rate hike of 25 basis points in December." SUJAN HAJRA, CHIEF ECONOMIST, ANAND RATHI, MUMBAI "The RBI's hike was, in our assessment, a touch-and-go decision shaped by extraordinary circumstances. Resilient domestic growth provided room to act, while rising food prices, elevated global crude prices, higher global and domestic bond yields, and rupee depreciation weighed heavily in favour of tightening." "This does not necessarily herald a series of further hikes: even the calibrated tightening stance leaves room for a pause, depending on how inflation and external pressures evolve." VIKRAM CHHABRA, SENIOR ECONOMIST, 360 ONE ASSET, MUMBAI "The decision reflects a broadening of price pressures and rising upside risks to the inflation outlook. Although kharif sowing has been broadly normal, the weak monsoon could hurt crop yields, while low reservoir levels in northern and southern India may weigh on rabi output. Further, if energy prices stay elevated, their pass-through to broader prices will follow with a lag. We therefore expect another 50 bps of rate hikes in this cycle." RADHIKA RAO, SENIOR ECONOMIST, DBS BANK, SINGAPORE "The RBI's October hike acknowledges that cyclical inflation risks are no longer benign. A change in stance also underscored the RBI MPC's hawkish intent. Against a backdrop of elevated oil prices, tighter global conditions, and risks to food inflation from unfavourable weather, policymakers have chosen to reinforce inflation credibility before risks become entrenched." GARIMA KAPOOR, DEPUTY HEAD OF RESEARCH AND ECONOMIST, ELARA SECURITIES, MUMBAI "Continuing commodity price pressures are likely to put upside pressure on inflation, as growth remains resilient, allowing quick pass-through of input prices to retail prices. The rising interest rate backdrop globally has also reduced RBI's degrees of freedom. We see (a) likelihood of another 50 bps (of) hike(s) this cycle."

item.title: India's Titan slips as festive timing dents September-quarter jewellery growth
item.description: Shares of Titan slid on Wednesday after the Indian retailer reported slower growth in its mainstay jewellery business for the September quarter, as a shift in the festive calendar delayed purchases.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shares of Titan (TITN.NS) slid on Wednesday after the Indian retailer reported slower growth in its mainstay jewellery business for the September quarter, as a shift in the festive calendar delayed purchases. The company's shares were down 4.3% at 4,359.80 rupees in early trade. Festival-related purchases that typically bolster sales were pushed to later in the year, deferring some consumer spending and softening demand toward the end of the quarter, analysts said. "We did not like the slowdown in buyer growth to mid-single digits (vs low double digits in 1Q and high single-digits in 4Q), sharp moderation in plain gold and coins, and CaratLane growth easing," Macquarie analysts said. The brokerage maintained a "buy" rating on the stock, with a target price of 5,600 rupees. Analysts at HSBC Global Investment Research said while the topline growth was underwhelming, the mix was positive with gold coin sales declining and studded jewellery growing faster, which are expected to have a positive impact on the company's margins. HSBC Global, which holds a "buy" rating and a target price of 5,510 rupees, said that beyond near-term concerns, the structural growth in the company's jewellery business remains strong. "The issue is more a case of circling higher base rather than any structural dent to Titan's growth outlook in our view," HSBC said.

item.title: India joins global rate-tightening wave with first hike in nearly 4 years
item.description: The Indian central bank raised its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% on Wednesday, marking the first rise in nearly four years amid mounting inflation and strong economic growth.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Kalra, Abinaya V
item.content:encoded: The Indian central bank raised its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% on Wednesday, marking the first rise in nearly four years amid mounting inflation and strong economic growth. The central bank also signalled further rate hikes by changing its stance from "neutral" to "calibrated tightening", but Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the extent and timing of any more increases would be contingent on actual inflation and growth outcomes. India has joined major central banks in raising rates as higher oil prices triggered by the Iran war fuel inflation, squeeze purchasing power and weigh on currencies. Weak monsoon rains linked to El Niño have compounded price pressures in Asia's third-largest economy. The six-member rate panel voted unanimously in favour of the rate hike. Nearly 60% of economists in a [USN:L4N45K09D TEXT:"Reuters poll"] had expected a 25 bps increase in the repo rate (INREPO=ECI) . "The Indian economy has been strong, and economic momentum remains broad based," Malhotra said, adding that the inflation outlook had worsened since the last policy meeting. There is some evidence of elevated inflation expectations and broadening of price pressures, Malhotra said. "It is clear that inflation and its outlook are not benign as they were last year." The RBI now expects inflation at 5.2%, a small increase over its earlier forecast of 5%. Core inflation is seen at 4.4% from 4.3% earlier. Analysts have been divided on how far the central bank will go in raising rates. "We expect another 50-75 basis point in rate hikes over the coming months," said Sakshi Gupta, economist at HDFC Bank. "In the event that the West Asia conflict lingers and oil prices remain elevated, the inflation risk could increase further, necessitating a more aggressive tightening cycle," Gupta said. India's benchmark 10-year bond yield was slightly higher at 7.2269%, while the rupee currency hovered around its previous close at 96.43 against the U.S. dollar. The benchmark Nifty 50 (.NSEI) Index was down 0.3% but recovered from day’s lows. HIGHER INFLATION, RESILIENT GROWTH Consumer inflation accelerated in August to 4.82% from a year earlier, above the Reserve Bank of India's 4% medium-term target for a third consecutive month. Higher prices of fuel and food are now [USN:L6N45K0J1 TEXT:"rippling"] through the economy, with nearly half of the consumer basket seeing inflation above 4%. "Headline CPI inflation is expected to average almost 5.8% in the next three quarters," Malhotra said. "In this milieu, recalibrating the policy rate is imperative". At the same time, economic growth remains strong, giving the central bank greater leeway to raise the cost of borrowing for consumers and businesses. The central bank expects GDP growth in the current financial year at 7.1%, 40 bps higher than its earlier projections. [USN:L4N44S0T4 TEXT:"GDP growth"] for the April-June quarter stood at 7.8%, well above the central bank's forecast of 7%. Malhotra said there is limited evidence of demand side pressures in inflation so far but risks exist "in view of strong growth in monetary and credit aggregates." India's bank credit growth has soared in the past few months and grew by 18.8% in October, reflecting strong demand. MANAGING LIQUIDITY Contrary to market expectations, the central bank refrained from announcing additional measures such as a hike in the reserve ratio to drain surplus liquidity from the banking system. "The Reserve Bank will use an appropriate mix of liquidity management tools," Malhotra said. Schemes to draw dollars and support the rupee drew close to $144 billion as of mid-September, according to central bank data. These dollars, swapped with the central bank, led to a flood of liquidity which peaked at a record 11.16 trillion rupees at the beginning of September. So far, the RBI has used bond sales and longer term FX swaps to drain liquidity. The lack of further measures was positive for Indian bank stocks, with the Nifty Bank Index up 0.15%, after dropping 0.7% earlier. “The RBI has taken a sensible first step with a 25-bps hike, our base case remains for 100 bps of cumulative tightening over this cycle," said Krishna Bhimavarapu, Asia pacific economist at State Street Investment Management in Bengaluru. "The ultimate magnitude will depend on how the global energy shock, food inflation broader inflation dynamics and the global tightening cycle evolve in the coming quarters," he said.

item.title: Morning Bid: Who's the boss?
item.description: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rocky Swift
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rocky Swift Wall Street indexes scaled new heights overnight on earnings optimism, but the buzz fizzled out in Asia as oil prices climbed again following [USN:L1N45T00S TEXT:"attacks"] by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia. To end a war that's roiled energy markets and stoked inflation for eight months, Iran must make a "meaningful" reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity, US Vice President JD Vance [USN:L6N45T01N TEXT:"told Reuters"]. But who's going to make that call? After waves of leaders in Tehran have exited the stage, nobody knows who is [USN:L1N45S12F TEXT:"running"] the country, according to US President Donald Trump . And speaking of leaders, if Marine Le Pen isn't the hero France deserves, she's the hero the nation's troubled bond market needed. The far-right candidate considered the frontrunner in next spring's presidential election outlined plans to [USN:L1N45S0C4 TEXT:"slash spending"], prompting a relief rally in French goverment bonds whose yields had surged to multi-decade highs. The enthusiasm spread to the euro and lent a tailwind to other bond markets, all under the common cloud of inflation, central bank tightening and fiscal woes. US Treasuries rebounded, aided by a solid 3-year [USN:L1N45S0T3 TEXT:"auction"], and the government is set to test market demand again with a $39 billion sale of 10-year notes later on Wednesday. Market focus now turns to the release of Federal Reserve minutes and speeches by its policymakers. Expectations for another rate increase this month after September's hike have retreated, but markets are still anticipating more tightening later in the year and next year. Speeches by San Francisco Fed President [USN:L6N45S13A TEXT:"Mary Daly"] and Kansas City Fed President [USN:S0N3XI00P TEXT:"Jeff Schmid"] on Tuesday offered a mixed picture on whether hikes will be needed sooner or later. Fed officials Christopher Waller, Neel Kashkari and Alberto Musalem are all due to speak later on Wednesday. The chance of a hike of at least 25 basis points in October stands at 20.5%, down from about 51% a week ago, according to CME FedWatch, but markets are pricing in an 84.5% chance of a hike at the December meeting. The pan-region Euro Stoxx 50 futures were down 0.62%, German DAX futures fell 0.55% and FTSE futures slid 0.25%. US stock futures, the S&P 500 e-minis , edged up 0.08%. Key developments that could influence markets on Wednesday: Germany industrial production (August) Canada leading index (September) US Treasury sells $39 billion of 10-year notes Germany reopening of 7-year government debt auction UK reopening of 1-year and 5-year government debt auctions US Fed publishes minutes of September 15-16 meeting Fed data on consumer credit

item.title: Boston Dynamics appoints ex-Amazon executive Rohit Prasad as CEO
